# Reference (generated by tools/gates/reference.py - do not edit)

Every file of the browser layer (`compat`), what it is for, and its public symbols. 
Symbols without a description have no `///` comment yet (tools/gates/check_docs.py lists them).

## `SpeedTreeRT.h`

SpeedTreeRT.h - OUR declaration of the `CSpeedTreeRT` interface: the contract between Ymir's `SpeedTreeLib` and our reader of baked trees (speedtree_web.cpp), written from USE alone - no SDK file is needed to build the client.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| class | `CSpeedTreeRT` | The SpeedTree RT 1.6 engine as Ymir's wrapper uses it: a baked mesh shared by the instances (`MakeInstance`), one position per instance, LOD always 1.0, no wind. See speedtree_web.cpp. |

## `amstream.h`

amstream.h - a redirect to the compatibility layer. A header TMP4 code pulls in directly. In Win32 it belongs to the `windows.h` family; here its content lives in `win32_compat.h`.

## `amvideo.h`

amvideo.h - DirectShow. Film playback in the Windows client. In the browser the <video> tag does that, so the DirectShow layer has nothing to play. The header is empty; when code reaches for a specific interface, the compiler will report it and it will be a separate decision.

## `codepages.cpp`

codepages.cpp - the CP1250 / CP1252 / CP874 tables and the string conversions (see codepages.h for the design). Table sources - the official Unicode/Microsoft mappings: CP1250: https://unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/VENDORS/MICSFT/WINDOWS/CP1250.TXT CP1252: https://unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/VENDORS/MICSFT/WINDOWS/CP1252.TXT CP874:  https://unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/VENDORS/MICSFT/WINDOWS/CP874.TX

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_CodePageKnown` | Whether this code page has a table here. *(from codepages.h)* |
| function | `M2W_ByteToChar` | One code-page byte -> one Unicode character.  Returns `0xFFFD` (the replacement character) for bytes the page does not assign. Such bytes exist in each of the three pages and must not be pretended to mean something. Unknown code page: also `0xFFFD`. *(from codepages.h)* |
| function | `M2W_CharToByte` | Unicode character -> one code-page byte.  Returns `false` when the page has no such character and then leaves `puByte` untouched. That is an ordinary situation: page 1252 has no Polish a with ogonek (U+0105). `0xFFFD` is never found (design note above). *(from codepages.h)* |
| function | `M2W_ToUtf16` | Code page -> UTF-16. Returns the number of 16-bit units written (or needed), zero on failure.  Failure means: unknown page, null pointer, buffer too small. An unassigned byte is NOT a failure - it becomes `0xFFFD`. *(from codepages.h)* |
| function | `M2W_FromUtf16` | UTF-16 -> code page. Returns the number of bytes written (or needed), zero on failure.  A character the page does not have becomes a question mark (`'?'`) and the conversion goes on - as Windows did. That is NOT a failure: a string in another language should come out readable where it can.  Surrogate pairs (characters outside the basic plane) also become a question mark - ONE per pair, not two. *(from codepages.h)* |

## `custom_draw.cpp`

custom_draw.cpp - road B: the shader program, the state memory, the draw calls, and two probes that run without a server (model probe with the canvas-hash gate, texture probe). See custom_draw.h.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_ForgetCustomState` | Tells the custom road that the OpenGL state changed outside it. The compatibility layer calls this before its own drawing - see the body. *(from custom_draw.h)* |
| function | `M2W_SetCustomFog` | Fog of road B: D3DFOG_* mode (0 off), start, end, density, RGB colour 0..1. *(from custom_draw.h)* |

| function | `M2W_DrawMeshFromBuffers` | Draws `uIndices` indices from buffers already on the card with our own program - see the declaration in custom_draw.h for every parameter. ## `custom_draw.h`

custom_draw.h - DRAWING PAST THE FIXED-FUNCTION PIPELINE ("road B"): one shader program, own buffers and own state for the spatial content (models), while the interface stays on the Direct3D 8 emulation.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| struct | `TVertexPNT` | The vertex the models are drawn with. EXACTLY the `PNT332` layout TMP4 uses for characters - position, normal, texture coordinates. |
| function | `M2W_DrawMesh` | Draws one mesh with the custom shader program.  @param c_pVertices   an array of `uVertices` vertices @param c_puIndices   triangle indices (three per triangle) @param uTexture      OpenGL texture name; 0 means "no texture" @param c_afWorld     4x4 world matrix, row-major (as in Direct3D) @param c_afView      4x4 view matrix @param c_afProjection 4x4 projection matrix |
| function | `M2W_DrawMeshFromBuffers` | Draws a mesh from BUFFERS already on the card.  Direct3D 8 buffers in this port ARE OpenGL buffers (`CGlBuffer` keeps the GL name beside the copy in memory). So when the game has already prepared the vertices and indices there is nothing to copy - bind and draw.  @param uStride        distance between vertices; MUST be the PNT layout @param uBaseVertex    `BaseVertexIndex` from `SetIndices` (in vertices) @param uIndexType     `GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT` or `GL_UNSIGNED_INT` @param uFirstIndex    number of the first index (in indices, not bytes) @param iBlend         non-zero when drawing with alpha blending (then no depth writes); M2W_BLEND_OFF = opaque @param iCull          M2W_CULL_NONE / M2W_CULL_CW / M2W_CULL_CCW @param iAlphaFunc     D3DCMP_* (1..8), M2W_ALPHA_TEST_OFF = no alpha test @param fAlphaRef      the alpha test reference, 0..1; ignored when the test is off (M2W_ALPHA_REF_UNUSED) |
| function | `M2W_DrawModelCustom` | ENTRY FOR THE GAME: draws what the game has just asked to draw - but by our road, not the fixed-function pipeline.  Takes EVERYTHING from the current device state (stream, indices, the texture of stage zero, world, view and projection matrices), so at the call site it is enough to replace `DrawIndexedPrimitive` with this. Returns `false` when the state is not fit for drawing our way - then the caller draws the old way.  Defined in `gl_device.cpp`, because the device state lives there. |
| function | `M2W_ClipHalfPixel` | Half a physical pixel of the device's current viewport in clip units - the pixel-centre fix the D3D8 road puts into its matrix, so that meshes drawn here stay on the same pixels as the terrain. The y component is mirrored on a flipped render target, because this road's projection arrives already flipped. Zeros without a device. Defined in `gl_device.cpp`. |
| function | `M2W_SetCustomFog` | Fog of road B: D3DFOG_* mode (0 off), start, end, density, RGB colour 0..1. |
| function | `M2W_ForgetCustomState` | Tells the custom road that the OpenGL state changed outside it. The compatibility layer calls this before its own drawing - see the body. |
| function | `M2W_ModelProbe` | PROBE: loads one `.gr2` model and draws N animated instances of it in rows of ten, with the camera orbiting them (it also runs the texture probe, `M2W_TextureProbe`, which has its own address switch).  Why: the whole road - reader, pose, deformation, drawing - can then be checked WITHOUT A SERVER, on the login screen. When the character appears the chain is whole and only the hook into the place where the game draws characters remains. When it does not, the fault is in the chain, not in what cannot be seen.  Switched on with `?modelprobe=N` in the page address, N = the number of characters - pose and skin are computed for them EVERY FRAME, as in the game. `?probehash=F` prints a hash of the canvas after the F-th probe frame (the gate `tools/gates/check_probe.py`). |
| function | `M2W_TextureProbe` | TEXTURE PROBE: loads a whole directory of images by the road the game takes and measures how long it takes. Answers whether the multi-second pauses come from uploading textures to the card.  Switched on with `?textureprobe=<directory>` or `?textureprobe=1` |

## `d3d8.h`

d3d8.h - the Direct3D 8 CONSTANTS AND TYPES layer for the port. MEASUREMENT: `GameLib` uses **116 constant names, 6 structure types and 6 interface names** of Direct3D - and not a single call of a device method. That is no accident: `GameLib` does not draw itself, it sets state through `CStateManager` from `EterLib`. `eterLib/StateManager.cpp` is compiled as it is, and the device it talks to is th

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| macro | `D3DCOLOR_ARGB` | Packs four 0-255 channels into a `D3DCOLOR` (A8R8G8B8); each argument is masked to its low 8 bits. |
| macro | `D3DCOLOR_RGBA` | `D3DCOLOR_ARGB` with the arguments in r, g, b, a order. |
| macro | `D3DCOLOR_XRGB` | `D3DCOLOR_ARGB` with alpha fixed at 0xFF (opaque). |
| struct | `IDirect3DResource8` | Base of every Direct3D resource: reference counting only. The destructor is protected - a resource goes away through `Release`. |
| struct | `IDirect3DSurface8` | A surface (render target, depth buffer or one mip level of a texture): description and CPU locking. Implemented by `CGlSurface` and `CGlLevelSurface` (gl_internal.h). |
| struct | `IDirect3DBaseTexture8` | Hierarchy kept as in the original: `EffectLib` passes a texture where the base type is expected. |
| struct | `IDirect3DTexture8` | A 2D texture with mip levels: per-level surfaces, locking and descriptions. Implemented by `CGlTexture` (gl_internal.h). |
| struct | `IDirect3DVertexBuffer8` | A vertex buffer: lock a byte range for writing, unlock to hand it to the GPU. Implemented by `CGlVertexBuffer` (gl_internal.h). |
| struct | `IDirect3DIndexBuffer8` | An index buffer, with the same lock/unlock contract as the vertex buffer. Implemented by `CGlIndexBuffer` (gl_internal.h). |
| struct | `IDirect3DDevice8` | The Direct3D 8 device: the methods TMP4 calls (measured and 155), pure virtual. Implemented by `CGlDevice` (gl_internal.h, gl_*.cpp); the destructor is protected - it goes away through `Release`. |
| struct | `_D3DCAPS8` | Device capabilities - the fields TMP4 reads, not Microsoft's layout (see above). Filled by `M2W_GlCapabilities` (gl_device.cpp), which both `CGlDevice::GetDeviceCaps` and the factory's `GetDeviceCaps` call. |
| macro | `D3DVS_VERSION` | Shader version number, as in D3D8: the kind tag in the high word, the major and minor version in the low one. |
| macro | `D3DPS_VERSION` | Pixel shader version number: `D3DVS_VERSION` with the pixel kind tag 0xFFFF in the high word. |
| struct | `_D3DMATRIX` | Direct3D matrix. `D3DXMATRIX` from `d3dx8.h` DERIVES from it - as in the original - so the field layout is the same and the conversion costs nothing. |
| struct | `_D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS_` | Presentation parameters passed to `CreateDevice` and `Reset`: back buffer size, format and count, swap effect, window, depth buffer. |
| macro | `D3DFVF_TEXCOORDSIZE1` | `FVF` bits saying that coordinate set `i` has one float. |
| macro | `D3DFVF_TEXCOORDSIZE2` | Two floats for set `i` - the default, whose code is 0, so the macro ignores `i`. |
| macro | `D3DFVF_TEXCOORDSIZE3` | `FVF` bits saying that coordinate set `i` has three floats. |
| macro | `D3DFVF_TEXCOORDSIZE4` | `FVF` bits saying that coordinate set `i` has four floats. |
| macro | `D3DVSD_STREAM` | Declaration token: the following registers come from stream `n`. |
| macro | `D3DVSD_REG` | Declaration token: input register `reg` takes data of type `t` (`D3DVSDT_*`) from the current stream. |
| macro | `D3DVSD_END` | Declaration token that ends the array (`0xFFFFFFFF`, kind 7). |
| struct | `IDirect3D8` | Direct3D 8 factory: adapter enumeration, format checks, caps and device creation, pure virtual. Implemented by `CGlFactory` (d3d8_factory.cpp). |
| function | `Direct3DCreate8` | `Direct3DCreate8` of the original API: the port's factory (d3d8_factory.cpp, `CGlFactory`). `GrpDevice.cpp` called exactly this; the name stays because any file of the tree may ask for it. |

## `d3d8_fixedfunc.cpp`

d3d8_fixedfunc.cpp - composing GLSL from the Direct3D 8 fixed-function pipeline: the rules below are the DIRECT3D 8 SPECIFICATION rewritten in GLSL, every blend operation with the formula it used. See d3d8_fixedfunc.h.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_DefaultPipelineKey` | Resets the key to Direct3D 8's INITIAL state - not to plain zeros. The defaults are part of the contract: after `Reset` the driver had stage 0 at `MODULATE(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE)` and every later stage disabled. *(from d3d8_fixedfunc.h)* |
| function | `M2W_BuildVertexProgram` | Composes the vertex program. GLSL ES 3.00, i.e. WebGL 2. *(from d3d8_fixedfunc.h)* |
| function | `M2W_BuildPixelProgram` | Composes the pixel program. *(from d3d8_fixedfunc.h)* |
| function | `M2W_KeyHash` | A number that describes the key - for the cache of finished programs. Different keys may give the same hash; the cache must compare keys, not trust the hash. *(from d3d8_fixedfunc.h)* |

## `d3d8_fixedfunc.h`

d3d8_fixedfunc.h - the Direct3D 8 fixed-function pipeline as a shader generator: the INPUT (a pipeline key - the set of states that determines a program) and the two functions that compose GLSL from it. Pure - testable (d3d8_fixedfunc_test.cpp, tools/gates/check_glsl.py).

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| struct | `TTextureStage` | The state of one texture stage - the subset of `D3DTSS_*` that AFFECTS the program. Filtering and wrapping (`MINFILTER`, `ADDRESSU`) are not here: in OpenGL they belong to the texture or the sampler object, not to the program - a filter change has no right to rebuild a shader. |
| struct | `TPipelineKey` | Everything that determines a program. Two equal keys must give the same code - the program cache in the layer above stands on that. |
| function | `M2W_DefaultPipelineKey` | Resets the key to Direct3D 8's INITIAL state - not to plain zeros. The defaults are part of the contract: after `Reset` the driver had stage 0 at `MODULATE(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE)` and every later stage disabled. |
| function | `M2W_BuildVertexProgram` | Composes the vertex program. GLSL ES 3.00, i.e. WebGL 2. |
| function | `M2W_BuildPixelProgram` | Composes the pixel program. |
| function | `M2W_KeyHash` | A number that describes the key - for the cache of finished programs. Different keys may give the same hash; the cache must compare keys, not trust the hash. |

## `d3d8_fvf.cpp`

d3d8_fvf.cpp - decomposition of an FVF code and of a `D3DVSD_*` declaration into a vertex layout. See d3d8_fvf.h.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_VertexLayout` | Decomposes an FVF code into a vertex layout. *(from d3d8_fvf.h)* |
| function | `M2W_LayoutFromDeclaration` | The same from a `D3DVSD_*` DECLARATION instead of an FVF code.  WHY: Direct3D 8 had two ways to describe a vertex - one number (FVF) or a run of `D3DVSD_*` words, which could also split the data over several streams. `CGraphicDevice` uses the latter for CHARACTER MODELS (`CreatePNTStreamVertexShader` and three sisters), and `SetVertexShader` then gets only the handle. Earlier our layer THREW those declarations AWAY: `CreateVertexShader` returned a handle with the top bit set, `SetVertexShader` saw that bit and left the remembered FVF code alone - so a character model drew with whatever layout was left over from something else. Symptom: characters smeared across the screen, without one OpenGL error.  WHAT IT UNDERSTANDS. Stream ZERO. A `D3DVSD_STREAM(n)` word with `n != 0` switches to a stream we never supply - its data is skipped and `bKnown` becomes `false`, so the caller knows the layout is incomplete. Silent consent would be worse: the layout would look right with wrong offsets.  `c_pDeclaration` may be `NULL` - then `iPosition` comes out -1. *(from d3d8_fvf.h)* |

|---|---|---|

| function | `M2W_VertexLayout` | Decomposes an FVF code into a vertex layout. |
| function | `M2W_LayoutFromDeclaration` | The same from a `D3DVSD_*` DECLARATION instead of an FVF code.  WHY: Direct3D 8 had two ways to describe a vertex - one number (FVF) or a run of `D3DVSD_*` words, which could also split the data over several streams. `CGraphicDevice` uses the latter for CHARACTER MODELS (`CreatePNTStreamVertexShader` and three sisters), and `SetVertexShader` then gets only the handle. Earlier our layer THREW those declarations AWAY: `CreateVertexShader` returned a handle with the top bit set, `SetVertexShader` saw that bit and left the remembered FVF code alone - so a character model drew with whatever layout was left over from something else. Symptom: characters smeared across the screen, without one OpenGL error.  WHAT IT UNDERSTANDS. Stream ZERO. A `D3DVSD_STREAM(n)` word with `n != 0` switches to a stream we never supply - its data is skipped and `bKnown` becomes `false`, so the caller knows the layout is incomplete. Silent consent would be worse: the layout would look right with wrong offsets.  `c_pDeclaration` may be `NULL` - then `iPosition` comes out -1. |

## `d3d8_gl.h`

d3d8_gl.h - the Direct3D 8 device built on WebGL 2: its public entry points (create/destroy, capabilities, factory, measurement switches). The device itself is `CGlDevice` (gl_internal.h, gl_*.cpp). WHAT THIS IS The body of the `IDirect3DDevice8` interface that `d3d8.h` describes from measurement. The client calls these methods through `CStateManager`; here they turn into OpenGL ES 3 calls, i.e. W

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_GlCapabilities` | Hardware capabilities. Both the device and the factory call it - see the note at the definition (gl_device.cpp). |
| function | `M2W_CreateGlFactory` | The `IDirect3D8` factory - answers questions about display modes. `CGraphicBase::ms_lpd3d` has to get it, otherwise `CPythonSystem::GetDisplaySettings` reads from a null pointer. |
| function | `M2W_CreateGlDevice` | Creates the device bound to the page's canvas.  `c_szCanvas` is a selector like `"#canvas"`. Returns NULL when WebGL 2 is not available - and that is a true answer, not a crash: there are browsers and machines without it. |
| function | `M2W_DestroyGlDevice` | Destroys the device and everything that belongs to it. |
| function | `M2W_ProgramCacheSize` | How many programs sit in the cache. For measurement and tests - the measurement says there should be a few dozen keys, not thousands. If this number grows without end, the key contains something that should not tell programs apart. |
| function | `M2W_ForceDxtDecode` | Forces the FALLBACK road for DXT textures - decoding in wasm instead of handing the blocks to the card.  It exists so that this road can be MEASURED where the browser has `WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc` and would never reach for it by itself. Without this switch the fallback would be code that runs only for people for whom nobody checks it - exactly where untested code must not be.  Called with `false` it hands the decision back to the browser. No caller in the repository (the test that used it was removed) - kept as a measurement hook. |

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_BytesPerPixel` | Bytes per pixel of the format. Zero for formats not handled here or without a fixed size (DXT). *(from d3d8_pixels.h)* |

| function | `M2W_ConvertPixelRect` | Copies a rectangle of pixels with format conversion and scaling.  `bLinear` chooses between the nearest source pixel and the average of four - `D3DX_FILTER_NONE` and `D3DX_FILTER_LINEAR`, the only two the client uses.  Returns `false` when either format is not handled - the true answer. A silent no-op would leave the texture full of zeros, a black rectangle instead of the image. |

## `d3d8_states.cpp`

d3d8_states.cpp - translation of Direct3D 8 constants into OpenGL ES 3. See d3d8_states.h for the three traps; the reasons sit at the cases.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_TextureFormat` | Direct3D pixel format -> description for OpenGL. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_BlendFactor` | Blend factor `D3DBLEND_*` -> `GL_*`. Returns `GL_ONE` for an unknown one, the value that distorts the image the least. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_BlendOp` | `D3DRS_BLENDOP` -> OpenGL blend equation.  Checked, because it looked like a trap and is not: Direct3D computes `D3DBLENDOP_SUBTRACT` as `source - destination`, exactly what `GL_FUNC_SUBTRACT` does; `D3DBLENDOP_REVSUBTRACT` is `destination - source`, i.e. `GL_FUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT`. The names correspond one to one and must NOT be swapped. Written down precisely because a reflexive "they are probably reversed" would cost one swap too many. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_CompareFunc` | Comparison `D3DCMP_*` -> `GL_*` (for the depth test). *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_CullMode` | Face culling. Returns through pointers, because in OpenGL these are TWO things - whether to cull and which side - and in Direct3D one. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_MinFilter` | Filtering. `dwMip` may be `D3DTEXF_NONE` - then there are no mip levels and the minification filter is plain, without `MIPMAP`. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_MagFilter` | Magnification: `GL_LINEAR` or `GL_NEAREST`, mip levels play no part. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_WrapMode` | Texture coordinate wrapping. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_PrimitiveMode` | Primitive type -> OpenGL mode. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_VerticesFromPrimitives` | Number of PRIMITIVES -> number of VERTICES. See trap 3. Returns 0 for an unknown type - better to draw nothing than garbage from the memory beside the buffer. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_ColorToFloat` | Splits a Direct3D colour (0xAARRGGBB) into four components 0..1. Separate, because `D3DRS_TEXTUREFACTOR` (57 uses) and the fog colour come in that form and the shader wants a `vec4`. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |
| function | `M2W_SwizzlePixels` | Converts a pixel buffer from the Direct3D layout to OpenGL's.  Source and target are SEPARATE, because the source buffer belongs to the client and must not be damaged - the client keeps textures in the `D3DPOOL_MANAGED` pool and may upload them again after a lost context.  Takes the WHOLE format description, not the swizzle kind alone: the pixel size is a property of the format, not of the swizzle, and separating them was an occasion for inconsistency.  For a compressed format does NOTHING - DXT blocks are not converted, they go to the card as they are. *(from d3d8_states.h)* |

## `d3d8caps.h`

d3d8caps.h - a redirect to our layer (like d3d8types.h).

## `d3d8types.h`

d3d8types.h - a redirect to our layer. The EterLib headers pull in `<d3d8types.h>` separately. Without this file they would hit Microsoft's original in `extern/include`, which would redefine structures `d3d8.h` already provides - and the compiler would rightly report it.

## `d3dtypes.h`

d3dtypes.h - a redirect to our layer (like d3d8types.h). A header from the DirectDraw days, pulled in by `EterImageLib`. The original in `extern/include` refers to `LPDDSURFACEDESC`, i.e. to the whole DirectDraw layer - while all that is needed from it are the pixel-format constants, which we have in `d3d8.h`.

## `d3dx8.h`

d3dx8.h - the D3DX8 MATHS layer for the port. THE MEASUREMENT behind this file: the whole of `GameLib` (59 files) uses **six types, one constant and 24 functions** of D3DX - nothing more. `D3DXVECTOR3` alone occurs 448 times, `D3DXMATRIX` 68. This is category B (algorithms and constants): it can be written from scratch and **checked by its properties**, without knowing Microsoft's original code. C

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| macro | `D3DXToRadian` | Degrees to radians (`degree * pi / 180`), as a float expression. |
| macro | `D3DXToDegree` | Radians to degrees (`radian * 180 / pi`), as a float expression. |
| struct | `D3DXVECTOR2` | Two-component float vector with the D3DX operators (component-wise add/subtract, scaling by a scalar, exact comparison). Converts to `float*` pointing at `x`. |
| struct | `D3DXVECTOR3` | Derives from `D3DVECTOR` in `d3d8.h`, as in the original. Without that, TMP4 code could not pass a `D3DVECTOR` where a `D3DXVECTOR3` is expected - and it does (`EterGrnLib` passes Granny's vertices directly). It adds no fields of its own, so it is still three `float`s. |
| struct | `D3DXVECTOR4` | Four-component float vector with the D3DX operators (component-wise add/subtract, scaling, exact comparison; no `/=`). Converts to `float*` pointing at `x`. |
| struct | `D3DXQUATERNION` | Quaternion. Field order `x y z w` - imaginary part BEFORE the real one, as in D3DX. TMP4 code builds quaternions with an initialiser list, so the reverse order would silently twist the rotations. |
| struct | `D3DXMATRIX` | Derives from `D3DMATRIX` in `d3d8.h`, as in the original. It adds no fields of its own, so the memory layout is the same, and passing a `D3DXMATRIX` where a `D3DMATRIX` is expected costs nothing. |
| struct | `D3DXPLANE` | Plane `a*x + b*y + c*z + d = 0`, stored as four floats in that order. Only construction, `float*` conversion and exact comparison - the maths is in the `D3DXPlane*` functions below. |
| struct | `D3DXCOLOR` | Derives from `D3DCOLORVALUE`, as in the original. |
| function | `D3DXVec2Dot` | Dot product of two 2D vectors. |
| function | `D3DXVec2Normalize` | Writes `v / \|v\|` to `out` and returns `out`; a zero vector gives zero. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Add` | `out = v1 + v2`; returns `out`. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Subtract` | `out = v1 - v2`; returns `out`. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Dot` | Dot product of two 3D vectors. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Cross` | `out = v1 x v2` (cross product); `out` may alias either input. |
| function | `D3DXVec3LengthSq` | Squared length `x*x + y*y + z*z` (no square root). |
| function | `D3DXVec3Length` | Euclidean length of a 3D vector. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Normalize` | Writes `v / \|v\|` to `out` and returns `out`; a zero vector gives zero, as in `D3DXVec2Normalize`. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Scale` | `out = v * s`; returns `out`. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Lerp` | Linear interpolation `out = v1 + s * (v2 - v1)`; `s` is not clamped. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Transform` | Full transform: `(v, 1) * M`, WITHOUT dividing by w. |
| function | `D3DXVec3TransformCoord` | Point: `(v, 1) * M`, divided by w. |
| function | `D3DXVec3TransformNormal` | Direction: `(v, 0) * M` - the translation does NOT apply. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixIdentity` | Sets `out` to the 4x4 identity matrix; returns `out`. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixMultiply` | `out = m1 * m2`. In the row convention this means "first m1, then m2". |
| function | `D3DXMatrixTranspose` | `out = transpose(mtx)`; `out` may alias `mtx`. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixTranslation` | Translation matrix: identity with `(x, y, z)` in the fourth row. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixScaling` | Scaling matrix: identity with `(sx, sy, sz)` on the diagonal. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixRotationX` | Rotation by `angle` radians about the X axis (row-vector form). |
| function | `D3DXMatrixRotationY` | Rotation by `angle` radians about the Y axis (row-vector form). |
| function | `D3DXMatrixRotationZ` | Rotation by `angle` radians about the Z axis (row-vector form). |
| function | `D3DXMatrixRotationQuaternion` | Quaternion -> rotation matrix in the ROW convention (i.e. the transpose of the textbook rotation matrix, which assumes a column vector). |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionRotationYawPitchRoll` | Forward declaration - defined below with the quaternions. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixRotationYawPitchRoll` | Rotation matrix from yaw/pitch/roll, built through the quaternion of `D3DXQuaternionRotationYawPitchRoll` so the two always agree. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixLookAtRH` | Right-handed view matrix. `zaxis` points FROM the target TO the eye - hence `eye - at`. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixOrthoRH` | Right-handed orthographic projection. The depth range is [0,1] (Direct3D), NOT [-1,1] (OpenGL) - a difference that the move to WebGL has to account for in ONE place, and not here. |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionMultiply` | MIND THE ORDER. D3DX documents this as `out = q2 * q1` in mathematical notation, which means "first rotation q1, then q2". That way the argument order is THE SAME as for `D3DXMatrixMultiply`.  This is not a guess - `d3dx8_math_test.cpp` checks that both paths AGREE: `R(QuaternionMultiply(q1,q2))` must equal `MatrixMultiply(R(q1),R(q2))`. The reverse order fails that test. |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionIdentity` | Sets `out` to the identity quaternion `(0, 0, 0, 1)`; returns `out`. |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionLength` | Length of the quaternion as a four-component vector. |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionNormalize` | Writes `q / \|q\|` to `out`; a zero quaternion gives the IDENTITY (not zero, unlike the vector normalisers). |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionRotationAxis` | The axis does NOT have to be normalised - D3DX normalises it itself. |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionRotationYawPitchRoll` | Quaternion from yaw (about Y), pitch (about X) and roll (about Z), in radians, composed in the order roll -> pitch -> yaw. |
| function | `D3DXPlaneDotCoord` | Product with a POINT: `a*x + b*y + c*z + d`. The sign says which side of the plane the point lies on - view culling in `GameLib` rests on this. |
| function | `D3DXPlaneDotNormal` | Product with a DIRECTION: without the constant term. |
| function | `D3DXPlaneNormalize` | Scales the WHOLE quadruple so that `(a,b,c)` has length 1. Normalising `(a,b,c)` alone, without `d`, would move the plane - a typical mistake. |
| function | `D3DXQuaternionConjugate` | Quaternion conjugate: a rotation by the same angle the OTHER way. For a unit quaternion it is also the inverse. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixDeterminant` | Determinant of a 4x4 matrix, expanded along the first row. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixfDeterminant` | `EterLib` calls this name with a lower-case `f` - that is how it is in the D3DX8 headers. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixOrthoOffCenterRH` | Orthographic projection given by its edges rather than width and height - allows a view volume that is NOT symmetric about the view axis. Depth lands in [0,1], as in Direct3D. |
| function | `D3DXGetFVFVertexSize` | Vertex size in bytes from its `FVF` description.  The number of texture coordinate sets sits in bits 8-11, and the size of EACH set - in the bits from 16 upwards, two per set. The default `00` means TWO numbers (8 bytes), not zero - this is where it is easy to count half as much as needed. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixPerspectiveFovRH` | Right-handed perspective projection. `fovY` is the **whole** vertical angle, not half of it - hence `1 / tan(fovY / 2)`. Depth lands in [0,1] (Direct3D), not [-1,1] (OpenGL); the conversion for WebGL is done in one place in the graphics layer, not here. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixInverse` | Matrix inverse by cofactors.  `pDeterminant` may be `NULL` - as in D3DX. For a singular matrix it returns `NULL` and **does not touch** `out`; TMP4 code checks the result, so silently returning garbage would be worse than having no function. |
| function | `D3DXMatrixRotationAxis` | Rotation matrix about an arbitrary axis. Built through a quaternion so that it is **by definition consistent** with `D3DXQuaternionRotationAxis` - computing it separately with Rodrigues' formula would let a convention mismatch show up only in the game. |
| function | `D3DXVec4Transform` | Full transform of a four-component vector: `v * M`, without the divide. `EterGrnLib` passes vertices with bone weights this way. |
| function | `D3DXVec2Length` | Euclidean length of a 2D vector. |
| function | `D3DXVec2CCW` | Cross product in the plane: positive when v2 lies to the left of v1. The name comes from "counter-clockwise" - the sign tells the winding. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Project` | Projects a point from the world to the screen. Mind y: on the screen it grows DOWNWARDS, hence the subtraction instead of addition. |
| function | `D3DXVec3Unproject` | The reverse path. For a singular matrix it leaves the result UNTOUCHED - just like D3DXMatrixInverse. |
| struct | `ID3DXMatrixStack` | D3DX matrix stack: push/pop plus the D3DX transform operations on the top matrix. Implemented in `d3dx8_matrixstack.cpp`; the destructor is protected, so it is released only through `Release`. |
| function | `D3DXCreateMatrixStack` | `D3DXCreateMatrixStack` of the original API; `CGraphicDevice::Create` (grpdevice_gl.cpp) calls it once. *(from d3dx8_matrixstack.cpp)* |
| function | `D3DXCreateTexture` | D3DX: creates a texture through the device; `D3DX_DEFAULT` mip levels means "down to one pixel", as Direct3D counted it. *(from d3dx8_textures.cpp)* |
| function | `D3DXCreateTextureFromFileInMemoryEx` | D3DX: image file in memory -> texture. Called for everything that is not a DDS (item icons, interface images, guild marks); the file is read by d3d8_image.cpp (TGA, BMP, JPEG, uncompressed DDS - tested), the rest of the D3DX contract is here: colour key, `D3DX_DEFAULT` size and format, every mip level computed from the ORIGINAL image (not from the previous level - rounding errors through eight halvings show on the smallest levels as a hue shift). *(from d3dx8_textures.cpp)* |
| function | `D3DXLoadSurfaceFromSurface` | D3DX: copies one whole surface into another with format conversion. Partial rectangles are not used by the client (all six calls in `GrpImageTexture.cpp` pass NULL); a compressed source is refused (see the design note). *(from d3dx8_textures.cpp)* |
| function | `D3DXAssembleShaderFromFileA` | The file variant: refuses, says so once per file name, and hands the message back in `ppCompilationErrors`. *(from d3dx8_shader.cpp)* |
| function | `D3DXAssembleShader` | The same assembler, but from MEMORY, not a file. SpeedTree uses it: its shaders are pasted into `VertexShaders.h` as strings in Direct3D 8 assembly. The answer is the same refusal, for the same reason - see `compat/d3dx8_shader.cpp`. |
| function | `D3DXCreateSphere` | Declared only - no body. Its only caller, the original `eterLib/GrpDevice.cpp`, is replaced by `grpdevice_gl.cpp`, which does not create the helper meshes. |
| function | `D3DXCreateCylinder` | Declared only - no body; same reason as `D3DXCreateSphere`. |
| struct | `ID3DXMesh` | D3DX mesh. Five methods - as many as `CScreen::RenderD3DXMesh` calls. `CGraphicBase` holds two such meshes (sphere and cylinder) for helper drawing, so the type has to be complete. |
| struct | `ID3DXBuffer` | D3DX buffer - a wrapper around a piece of memory returned by the shader assembler and by mesh creation. |
| function | `D3DXColorModulate` | Per-component colour product - channel by channel, alpha included. Used when dimming interface elements. |

## `d3dx8math.h`

d3dx8math.h - a redirect to our maths layer.

## `ddraw.h`

ddraw.h - DirectDraw. Pulled in by `EterImageLib`. DirectDraw was the 2D drawing layer of the 90s, already dropped in DirectX 8 in favour of Direct3D. `EterImageLib` pulls this header in for the pixel-format constants alone - and those are already in `d3d8.h`.

## `ddstream.h`

ddstream.h - a redirect to the compatibility layer. A header TMP4 code pulls in directly. In Win32 it belongs to the `windows.h` family; here its content lives in `win32_compat.h`.

## `devil_web.cpp`

devil_web.cpp - DevIL, but only as much as the client really calls: the fourteen `il*` functions the guild-mark code uses, over the image reader of d3d8_image.cpp and a 32-bit TGA writer.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `ilInit` | DevIL: resets the store. |
| function | `ilShutDown` | DevIL: frees every image. |
| function | `ilGenImages` | DevIL: allocates `Num` image ids. |
| function | `ilBindImage` | DevIL: selects the image the following calls act on. |
| function | `ilDeleteImages` | DevIL: frees images; a bound one is unbound. |
| function | `ilEnable` | DevIL: `IL_ORIGIN_SET` and `IL_FILE_OVERWRITE` are honoured; any other mode is acknowledged and reported (a refusal would stop the caller). |
| function | `ilOriginFunc` | DevIL: the reader always returns top-down; any other origin is reported and refused rather than silently flipped. |
| function | `ilLoad` | DevIL: loads a file into the bound image. The type argument is `IL_TYPE_UNKNOWN` in all five client calls ("detect yourself"); `M2W_LoadImage` detects by content, so it is unnamed. |
| function | `ilSave` | DevIL: saves the bound image - TGA only, as both `ilSave` calls in the tree pass `IL_TGA`; another format is refused, not written as TGA under a foreign name. |
| function | `ilTexImage` | DevIL: (re)allocates the bound image and copies `Data` in when given. |
| function | `ilSetPixels` | DevIL: writes a rectangle into the bound image, row by row with bounds checked on every pixel - marks are assembled from blocks placed into a larger board, so a rectangle outside the image is not unthinkable, and without the check it would be a write into foreign memory. |
| function | `ilCopyPixels` | DevIL: copies a rectangle out of the bound image; pixels outside the image come out as ZEROS, not memory garbage. Returns the pixels copied. |
| function | `ilConvertImage` | DevIL: the store ALWAYS holds `IL_BGRA` bytes (all four client calls ask for that), so no conversion is needed - only the CHECK that the request is for what we have. |
| function | `ilGetInteger` | DevIL: properties of the bound image. `IL_IMAGE_BITS_PER_PIXEL` returns the number of BYTES, as DevIL misleadingly does - the client relies on DevIL's behaviour, not on the name. |

dinput.h - DirectInput key codes. THE HISTORY OF THIS FILE is a lesson in itself. At first I made it **empty** and wrote that this was "from measurement, not an unfinished job" - because `GameLib` does not use DirectInput even once. That was true about `GameLib`. Then it turned out that `UserInterface` uses **118 different `DIK_*` codes**, in 236 places, and that 20 files do not compile without th

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| struct | `IDirectInputDevice8A` | A DirectInput device - interface only, no implementation (see above). |
| struct | `IDirectInput8A` | The DirectInput object - interface only, no implementation. |
| function | `DirectInput8Create` | Body in `platform_none.cpp`: sets `*ppvOut` to NULL and returns `E_FAIL` - input comes from DOM events, and an error (not an empty object) keeps TMP4 from calling methods on nothing. |

## `direct.h`

direct.h - a REDIRECT for the TMP4 port. TMP4 code includes this header directly. Instead of rewriting hundreds of #include directives, I provide a file with this name that pulls in our compatibility layer. That keeps the TMP4 sources UNTOUCHED - and the less we touch them, the easier it will be to take in fixes from upstream.

## `dshow.h`

dshow.h - DirectShow. Film playback in the Windows client. In the browser the <video> tag does that, so the DirectShow layer has nothing to play. The header is empty; when code reaches for a specific interface, the compiler will report it and it will be a separate decision.

| kind | symbol | description |

| function | `M2W_DxtByteCount` | Bytes a texture of this format and size occupies. Zero for a bad format or a size that is not a multiple of 4.  Separate because the caller needs the number BEFORE allocating - and the code that later reads the buffer had better be the code that sized it. *(from dxt.h)* |
| function | `M2W_DecodeDxt` | Decodes a whole texture to `0xAARRGGBB` pixels.  `c_pvBlocks` - compressed data, blocks left to right, then down (like the pixels). `uBytes`     - size of the block buffer; the function MUST NOT read past it. `iWidth`, `iHeight` - in pixels; both must be multiples of 4. `pauTarget`  - room for `iWidth * iHeight` 32-bit words, tightly packed, first image row first.  Returns `false` when something cannot be done - bad format, bad size, block buffer too small, null pointer. Nothing plausible-looking is written to the target in that case. *(from dxt.h)* |

## `frame_stats.cpp`

frame_stats.cpp - frame accounting (see frame_stats.h for the design).

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_BeginFrame` | Starts a frame. Called at the BEGINNING of a main-loop iteration.  Why a separate begin when there is an end: without it the account measured WALL time, report to report. At 60 FPS most of that is WAITING for the next frame, not work, and the "REST" line came out huge (923 ms of 1000 ms measured with twenty characters on screen) - looking like a large unknown cost in the game, while it was mostly idleness. Same family of mistake as above: a true number about the wrong thing. Now WORK is measured - time spent inside the iteration - and the waiting share is shown separately. *(from frame_stats.h)* |
| function | `M2W_MeasureFrame` | Ends a frame: every 60th (or every 5 s) prints the account and resets the counters. Called at the end of a main-loop iteration. *(from frame_stats.h)* |

## `gl_device.cpp`

gl_device.cpp - the Direct3D 8 device on WebGL 2: its life cycle (constructor, destructor, Present, Reset, TestCooperativeLevel), the hardware capabilities shared with the factory, and the M2W_* entry points (create/destroy the device, road B, program cache size, DXT switch). The rest of `CGlDevice` lives in gl_textures.cpp, gl_buffers.cpp, gl_shaders.cpp, gl_render_states.cpp and gl_render_target

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| EM_JS | `m2w_software_tnl` | `?tnl=0` - back to software vertex transformation. 1 = forced. |
| function | `M2W_GlCapabilities` | Hardware capabilities. Both the device and the factory call it - see the note at the definition (gl_device.cpp). *(from d3d8_gl.h)* |
| function | `M2W_ForceDxtDecode` | Forces the FALLBACK road for DXT textures - decoding in wasm instead of handing the blocks to the card.  It exists so that this road can be MEASURED where the browser has `WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc` and would never reach for it by itself. Without this switch the fallback would be code that runs only for people for whom nobody checks it - exactly where untested code must not be.  Called with `false` it hands the decision back to the browser. No caller in the repository (the test that used it was removed) - kept as a measurement hook. *(from d3d8_gl.h)* |
| function | `M2W_CreateGlDevice` | Creates the device bound to the page's canvas.  `c_szCanvas` is a selector like `"#canvas"`. Returns NULL when WebGL 2 is not available - and that is a true answer, not a crash: there are browsers and machines without it. *(from d3d8_gl.h)* |
| function | `M2W_DestroyGlDevice` | Destroys the device and everything that belongs to it. *(from d3d8_gl.h)* |
| function | `M2W_DrawModelCustom` | ENTRY FOR THE GAME: draws what the game has just asked to draw - but by our road, not the fixed-function pipeline.  Takes EVERYTHING from the current device state (stream, indices, the texture of stage zero, world, view and projection matrices), so at the call site it is enough to replace `DrawIndexedPrimitive` with this. Returns `false` when the state is not fit for drawing our way - then the caller draws the old way.  Defined in `gl_device.cpp`, because the device state lives there. *(from custom_draw.h)* |
| function | `M2W_ClipHalfPixel` | Half a physical pixel of the device's current viewport in clip units - the pixel-centre fix the D3D8 road puts into its matrix, so that meshes drawn here stay on the same pixels as the terrain. The y component is mirrored on a flipped render target, because this road's projection arrives already flipped. Zeros without a device. Defined in `gl_device.cpp`. *(from custom_draw.h)* |
| function | `M2W_ProgramCacheSize` | How many programs sit in the cache. For measurement and tests - the measurement says there should be a few dozen keys, not thousands. If this number grows without end, the key contains something that should not tell programs apart. *(from d3d8_gl.h)* |

## `gl_internal.h`

gl_internal.h - the ABI BETWEEN the `gl_*.cpp` files that together make up the WebGL device (`d3d8_gl.cpp` split into modules).

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| class | `CGlResource` | The common part: a reference count. Direct3D counts them itself, and the client relies on it - `Release()` appears 211 times in its code. |
| function | `GpuHasDxt` | The hardware's real answer (`g_iGpuHasDxt`), unless the measurement hook `M2W_ForceDxtDecode` has overridden it (the hook has no caller today; it is kept for measurements). |
| function | `M2W_ForgetGlState` | Tells the layer that somebody drew OUTSIDE it and its state memory no longer matches what is really set in OpenGL.  Called by `custom_draw.cpp` - the own drawing road for 3D content (user decision, "road B"). Without it the state memory would skip calls that are needed again after our work - and the image would lose transparency or depth in a way impossible to trace. Body in gl_render_states.cpp; `CGlDevice::SetRenderTarget` calls it too. |
| class | `CGlTexture` | `IDirect3DTexture8` on WebGL 2: every level keeps its own copy in wasm memory (principle one, gl_device.cpp), sent to the card on `UnlockRect` (`UploadLevel`). |
| class | `CGlSurface` | A surface is a **description** here, not memory. The client uses it only to ask for the size of the screen buffer (`GetBackBuffer`, `GetDepthStencilSurface`) and for comparisons. Nobody writes to it. |
| class | `CGlLevelSurface` | A view of ONE level of detail of a texture.  The client uses it in one place and for one thing: `GrpImageTexture.cpp` takes the source and target surfaces and has `D3DXLoadSurfaceFromSurface` copy one into the other - when shrinking textures and converting to a smaller format.  It is a **view**, not a copy: `LockRect` goes straight to the texture. A copy would mean that writing to the surface never reaches the texture - and the whole copy would silently do nothing.  The surface HOLDS a reference to the texture. Without it a client that releases the texture before the surface - which is exactly what `GrpImageTexture.cpp` does - would be left with a pointer to freed memory. |
| class | `CGlBuffer` | Common to the vertex and index buffer: a copy in wasm memory, sent to OpenGL on `Unlock`. |
| class | `CGlVertexBuffer` | `IDirect3DVertexBuffer8` on `CGlBuffer`. `FVF()` returns the vertex layout code given to `CreateVertexBuffer` - today with no caller in compat/ (the port's `IDirect3DVertexBuffer8` has no `GetFVF` in its interface, d3d8.h:529-535); the layout for drawing takes a separate path, through `CGlDevice::m_dwFVF`/`SetVertexShader`. |
| class | `CGlIndexBuffer` | `IDirect3DIndexBuffer8` on `CGlBuffer`; `GlType()`/`BytesPerIndex()` carry the index width (16 or 32 bits) chosen at creation. |
| struct | `TProgram` | A compiled program: the GL handle plus the locations of every input `CGlDevice` may need to send. `-1` (what `glGetUniformLocation`/ `glGetAttribLocation` return for a name they do not find) means "this program does not have it" - a shader may leave out inputs it does not use. |
| function | `CompileShader` | Compiles one shader (vertex or pixel) from GLSL source composed by `d3d8_fixedfunc.cpp`. Returns 0 and prints the whole source together with the error when the driver refuses - `FindOrBuildProgram` (gl_shaders.cpp) checks it explicitly (`if (!uVertexShader \|\| !uPixelShader) return NULL;`) before `glAttachShader`, so a zero never goes on silently. |
| class | `CGlDevice` | `IDirect3DDevice8` on WebGL 2 - the whole device the game draws on. The Direct3D state is recorded in arrays and applied to OpenGL only at draw time (principle three, gl_device.cpp header). |

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `MemberSize` | How many bytes ONE element of a member of this kind takes. For an inline member (`GrannyInlineMember`) computed recursively from the component's type description. *(from gr2_file.h)* |

## `granny.h`

granny.h - choosing the platform branch for the Granny 3D SDK. WHAT BREAKS WITHOUT THIS FILE: `extern/include/granny.h` starts with a ladder of platform detection - `_XENON`, `_GAMECUBE`, `NN_PLATFORM_CTR`, `__CELLOS_LV2__`, `_PSX2`, `_MSC_VER`... Emscripten is not on that list (the SDK is older), so **no branch fires** and the macros `GRANNY_DYNIMP`, `GRANNY_CALLBACK`, `granny_uint64x` stay undef

## `granny_pose.cpp`

granny_pose.cpp - poses, mesh binding and vertex deformation: what happens EVERY FRAME for every character (granny_web.cpp is what happens once, at load; curve sampling and controls are in granny_control.cpp).

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| EM_JS | `m2w_skin_shortcut` | `?skinshortcut=0` -> 0, anything else -> 1. |
| struct | `local_pose` | One transform per bone. |
| struct | `world_pose` | World and composite matrices per bone, FLAT, sixteen floats per bone: `granny_matrix_4x4` is a bare `float[4][4]`, which cannot go into a `std::vector` - an array has neither the constructor nor the destructor the container demands. The memory layout is identical, so the cast to `granny_matrix_4x4*` is honest, not a trick. |
| struct | `mesh_binding` | Which skeleton bone each mesh binding maps to. |
| struct | `mesh_deformer` | Input and output vertex layouts with the component offsets precomputed. |
| function | `GrannyInstantiateModel` | A new instance with clock 0, no controls, the initial placement as a matrix. |
| function | `GrannyFreeModelInstance` | The controls point at the instance - detached BEFORE it is freed. |
| function | `GrannyGetSourceSkeleton` | The skeleton of the instance's model. |
| function | `GrannySetModelClock` | Sets the instance clock (counted for the clock-rate measurement). |
| function | `GrannyUpdateModelMatrix` | ROOT MOTION. Earlier the matrix passed through untouched - and the character RAN ON THE SPOT: `CActorInstance::__AccumulationMovement` passes the character's rotation matrix here and reads the translation (`_41, _42, _43`) out of the result as movement in the world. The translation in model space comes from the controls (`M2W_RootMotion`, from the animation's `LoopTranslation`); here it is rotated by the source matrix (row times matrix, as everywhere in Granny) and added to its translation. |
| function | `GrannyNewLocalPose` | A local pose of `iBones` zeroed transforms. |
| function | `GrannyFreeLocalPose` | See `GrannyNewLocalPose`. |
| function | `GrannyNewWorldPose` | All matrices start as identity. |
| function | `GrannyFreeWorldPose` | See `GrannyNewWorldPose`. |
| function | `GrannyGetWorldPose4x4` | The world matrix of a bone; IDENTITY (not NULL) for a missing pose or bone - the caller reads sixteen numbers out of it and multiplies vertices by them, so a null pointer would turn a missing model into a crash. Identity means "a bone without a transform" and invents nothing. |
| function | `GrannyGetWorldPoseComposite4x4` | The composite (inverse-world * world) matrix of a bone; identity as above. |
| function | `GrannyGetWorldPose4x4Array` | All world matrices, contiguous; NULL for an empty pose. |
| function | `GrannyGetWorldPoseComposite4x4Array` | All composite matrices, contiguous; NULL for an empty pose. |
| function | `M2W_PoseTransforms` | The transforms of a local pose - `granny_pose.cpp` keeps them in a vector. *(from granny_internal.h)* |
| function | `GrannySampleModelAnimations` | Composes the pose from the animations playing on the instance (`granny_control.cpp`). A bone without a track gets the rest pose (once ALL of them did, because the controls were stubs). |
| function | `GrannyBuildWorldPose` | World matrices `local * parent` down the chain (the root gets the caller's offset), and composite = inverse-world * world, which the vertices are multiplied by: first from the rest pose into the bone's space, then to where the bone is now. |
| function | `GrannySampleModelAnimationsAccelerated` | The "accelerated" form: sample and compose in one pass. TMP4 calls this one and left the other commented out beside it.  WITHOUT THE MODEL'S INITIAL PLACEMENT - that was a CRUTCH. Earlier the root bone sat on `Model->InitialPlacement`, because without animation the player model's rest pose LAY DOWN: its `Bip01` has an identity local transform and the height and rotation come only with the ANIMATION TRACK (measured in the game: rest `(0 0 0)`, the `wait` animation gives `(2.2 -2.2 91.4)` with a rotation). The crutch added that height a second time - and the character hung a metre above the ground. Granny's `BuildWorldPose` composes ONLY the caller's offset; TMP4 never reads `InitialPlacement`. The same here: no offset = identity. ATTACHED things (weapon, hair) get the parent bone's matrix and that is the start of their chain. |
| function | `GrannyNewMeshBinding` | Maps every bone binding of the mesh to a bone of `c_pToSkeleton` by name. THE TABLE IS LONGER THAN NEEDED - ON PURPOSE.  A vertex holds binding numbers in BYTES, so it can give any number from 0 to 255. Granny's contract does not give the deformer the length of this table, so there is nothing to check there - the only place where that hole can be closed is HERE: the table always has at least 256 entries, and the surplus ones point at the root bone.  That this is not excess caution: measured on 400 corpus models - `triton_boss_lod_01` has 2641 vertices with a NON-ZERO weight at binding numbers 155-255, with 86 bindings. That file is damaged (44% of its normals are not unit length - see the open Oodle1 defect in `gr2_oodle1.h`), but the conclusion is general: DATA CAN BE BAD, and a reader in the client has no right to die of it. Without this padding it was "memory access out of bounds" and the client crashed. |
| function | `GrannyFreeMeshBinding` | See `GrannyNewMeshBinding`. |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshBindingToBoneIndices` | The binding -> skeleton bone table (at least 256 entries, see above). |
| function | `GrannyNewMeshDeformer` | Precomputes the component offsets of both layouts and the roles (position, normal) that get transformed. |
| function | `GrannyFreeMeshDeformer` | See `GrannyNewMeshDeformer`. |
| function | `GrannyDeformVertices` | Vertices through the bones - LINEAR BLENDING OF WEIGHTS.  `c_piMatrixIndices` says which SKELETON BONE corresponds to which mesh binding; a vertex holds binding numbers, not bones. That one indirection is the whole difference between "the mesh of the model" and "the mesh on this skeleton" - thanks to it the same mesh fits another skeleton, as long as the bones have the same names. |

## `granny_web.cpp`

granny_web.cpp - the Granny file API on our `.gr2` reader: loading (`GrannyReadEntireFileFromMemory`), access to meshes, materials, textures and bones, copying vertices and indices into the layout the caller asks for. Poses, mesh bindings and deformation are in granny_pose.cpp, animation control in granny_control.cpp.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `GrannySetLogCallback` | The one function that was here earlier. Reads and creates no data - tells the library where to print ITS OWN messages. There is no library, so there is nothing to redirect. |
| function | `GrannyConvertSingleObject` | Not written: the reader does its own conversion by name (gr2_to_granny). |
| function | `GrannyCopyMeshIndices` | Copies the triangle indices into the card's buffer at the requested width. The file may hold them sixteen- or thirty-two-bit and the card wants the one width the caller asks for - so both conversions exist. |
| function | `GrannyCopyMeshVertices` | Copies the vertices into the layout the caller asks for - BY COMPONENT NAME, not by offset.  This is the whole point of a format that carries a type description with its data. A vertex in the file may be `Position BoneWeights BoneIndices Normal UV` (40 bytes) while the card wants `Position Normal UV` (32 bytes) - and what goes where is decided by name. A component the file lacks is zeroed: better zero than somebody else's bytes. |
| function | `GrannyFindBoneByName` | Bone index by name, or false. |
| function | `GrannyFindMatchingMember` | Not written: reports once, returns false. |
| function | `GrannyFreeFile` | Frees the file - the sections AND the converted objects go with it. |
| function | `GrannyFreeFileSection` | TMP4 frees the sections with vertices and indices right after copying them into the card's buffers. The original may - we MUST NOT, and that is deliberate: the converted objects (`Indices`, `Vertices`) POINT INTO those sections instead of copying them. Copying would save memory only apparently, because it would first have to be doubled. So this function does nothing and says so once. Real memory saving comes with data streaming. |
| function | `GrannyGetFileInfo` | The converted `granny_file_info` of a loaded file. |
| function | `GrannyGetMaterialTextureByType` | The texture of a material for the given kind.  A material holds its texture in two ways: directly (`Texture`) or through named references (`Maps`, each with a `Usage`). In the corpus the models use the first, but the second is in the format and files from other servers may use it - so both are handled. |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshIndexCount` | The file carries indices EITHER thirty-two- OR sixteen-bit. |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshTriangleGroupCount` | Material groups of the mesh (one draw call each in TMP4). |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshTriangleGroups` | See `GrannyGetMeshTriangleGroupCount`. |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshVertexCount` | Vertices of the primary vertex data, 0 without one. |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshVertexType` | The vertex type description FROM THE FILE (TMP4 composes the FVF from it). |
| function | `GrannyGetMeshVertices` | The raw vertices in the file's layout - pointer into the section. |
| function | `GrannyGetTotalTypeSize` | The size of the TYPE DESCRIPTION ITSELF in bytes - not of the object. TMP4 divides the result by 32 (the size of one description row) and walks the component names to compose the FVF. The closing row is counted in, because TMP4 skips rows without a name anyway. |
| function | `GrannyMeshIsRigid` | A RIGID mesh is one whose vertices carry no bone weights. TMP4 splits the whole drawing path on that: rigid ones go straight into the card's buffer, deformed ones go through the pose. |
| function | `GrannyReadEntireFileFromMemory` | LOADING A `.gr2` FILE - everything else starts here.  The input buffer is NOT kept: the sections unpack into their own memory and the relocations are written in as real pointers. The caller may therefore free its buffer right after the return - and TMP4 does. |

## `platform_text.cpp`

platform_text.cpp - the GDI text functions `EterLib/GrpFontTexture.cpp` draws its glyph atlas with (CreateCompatibleDC, CreateDIBSection, CreateFontIndirect, SelectObject, GetCharABCWidthsFloatW, TextOutW...): baked GDI glyph bitmaps as the main road, a 2D canvas (runtime.js, m2w.text*) as the fallback, both ending in the DIB pixels TMP4 reads.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_create` | A 2D canvas of the given size; returns its index (m2w.textCanvasCreate). |

| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_measure` | Width of the string in the canvas font (m2w.textMeasure). |
| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_measure_three` | Width, left and right bounding box into `pdOut[3]` - one crossing instead of three; `GetCharABCWidthsFloatW` asks for whole character ranges. |
| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_measure_prefixes` | Cumulative widths of the prefixes of the string (real kerning). |
| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_bbox_right` | Right edge of the string's ink (m2w.textBboxRight). |
| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_height` | Ink height of the string (m2w.textHeight). |

| EM_JS | `m2w_canvas_read_rows` | Copies the rectangle [x0, x1) x [y0, y1) of the canvas into the DIB. |
| function | `CreateCompatibleDC` | GDI: a memory device context. |
| function | `CreateDIBSection` | GDI: a 32-bit bitmap with direct pixel access (`*ppvBits`). |
| function | `CreateFontIndirectA` | GDI: a font from a `LOGFONT` - the CSS string for the canvas and, when the package has it, the baked GDI font. |
| function | `SelectObject` | GDI: binds a font or bitmap to the context and returns the PREVIOUS one - TMP4 restores it after drawing. |
| function | `DeleteObject` | GDI: frees a bitmap (and its pixels) or a font. |
| function | `DeleteDC` | GDI: frees a memory context. |
| function | `SetTextColor` | GDI: text colour (BGR), returns the previous one. |
| function | `SetBkColor` | GDI: background colour (BGR), returns the previous one. |
| function | `SetBkMode` | GDI: OPAQUE / TRANSPARENT background, returns the previous mode. |
| function | `TextOutW` | GDI: draws the string into the DIB - baked glyphs when every character is baked (GDI road; at GUI scale into the shadow too), otherwise through the canvas. DIB pixels are BGRA; the engine reads blue (`& 0xff`), so the text colour goes in as the COLORREF (BGR). |
| function | `TextOutA` | GDI: `TextOutW` for a byte string. |
| function | `GetTextExtentPoint32W` | GDI: width of the string and the LINE height of the font (not of these characters: "___" and "ABC" must give the same height). |
| function | `GetTextExtentPoint32A` | GDI: `GetTextExtentPoint32W` for a byte string. |
| function | `GetCharABCWidthsFloatW` | GDI: the `ABC` triple per character - exact from the bake; from the canvas an APPROXIMATION derived from the total width and the bounding box, a fraction of a pixel off in the spacing, not an error. |
| function | `GetCharacterPlacementW` | GDI: only `lpDx` is implemented - the width of every character IN THE CONTEXT of the whole string (real kerning), the one field of this API the client uses. The rest of `GCP_RESULTSW` is zeroed: not needed, and faking it without a measurement would be guessing. |
| function | `SetDIBitsToDevice` | GDI: copying a bitmap TO THE SCREEN. The screen is drawn by the graphics layer, not GDI - this road leads nowhere and does not pretend to have drawn; the row count the caller expects is returned so it is not taken for a read error. |
| function | `M2W_FontAtlasHiRes` | The physical-pixel shadow of the DIB whose logical content equals the texture `c_pvData` (w x h, 16-bit) the engine is uploading, or NULL (gl_device.cpp swaps the texture for it; the engine copies the DIB to the texture 1:1 - `pwDst[x] = pdwSrc[x]`, the low 16 bits - so equality of the whole content identifies the DIB). |

## `python2_bridge.cpp`

python2_bridge.cpp - the bridge functions that do something at run time: module registration in `sys.modules`, strings across the code-page border, `Py_BuildValue`, and `PyErr_Print` that survives `SystemExit`.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `M2W_InitModule` | The counterpart of `Py_InitModule4` from Python 2: creates the module, puts it into `sys.modules` and returns it as a BORROWED reference, as the original did (the reference from `PyModule_Create` is never released, so the module survives even a cleared `sys.modules`, and TMP4 never calls `Py_DECREF` on the result - with 2 it did not have to). *(from python2_bridge.h)* |
| function | `M2W_BridgeCodePage` | The code page of the border: the game localisation's, else 1252. *(from python2_bridge.h)* |
| function | `M2W_PyStringN` | Code-page bytes of length `n` (-1 = NUL-terminated) -> str. *(from python2_bridge.h)* |
| function | `M2W_PyString` | Code-page bytes -> str (`PyString_FromString`). *(from python2_bridge.h)* |
| function | `M2W_PyBytes` | str -> code-page bytes (`PyString_AsString`); the buffer lives in a ring of the last 256 conversions - TMP4 uses it at once. *(from python2_bridge.h)* |
| function | `M2W_BuildValue` | `Py_BuildValue` with strings decoded in the code page. *(from python2_bridge.h)* |
| function | `M2W_PrintPythonError` | `PyErr_Print` that survives `SystemExit`: for `SystemExit` CPython's `PyErr_Print` calls `Py_Exit` - finalises the interpreter and ends the process. In the browser the "process" is the frame loop, which goes on: the window objects are dead, `UI::CWindow::m_poHandler` dangles and the next mouse move is `memory access out of bounds` (seen after `exception.Abort()` -> `sys.exit()` after a missing locale key). Here `SystemExit` ends the main loop through `PostQuitMessage` (as `CPythonApplication::Abort` does); every other error prints as before. Called from `ScriptLib/PythonUtils.cpp` (patched). *(from python2_bridge.h)* |

## `win32_compat.cpp`

win32_compat.cpp - the body of the compatibility layer: files and mappings on POSIX, the clock, `Sleep` as a deadline for the main loop, directories, the clipboard, global memory, GDI leftovers. See the header.

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| function | `FindMapping` | The live mapping at `addr`, or null. |
| function | `RememberMapping` | Records a mapping after `mmap`, so that `UnmapViewOfFile` knows its length. |
| function | `ForgetMapping` | Drops the record before `munmap`. |
| function | `CreateFileA` | POSIX `open`: GENERIC_READ/WRITE -> O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY/O_RDWR, CREATE_ALWAYS -> O_CREAT\|O_TRUNC; the path goes through `M2W_ResolvePathCase` (read) or `M2W_PosixPath` (write). INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE on error. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `CloseHandle` | `close` of the file descriptor; FALSE for INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE or NULL. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `ReadFile` | `read` up to `toRead` bytes; `*read` = bytes read (0 on error). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `WriteFile` | `write` of `toWrite` bytes; `*written` = bytes written (0 on error). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetFileSize` | `fstat` size - low 32 bits returned, high 32 in `*hi`; INVALID_FILE_SIZE on error. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `SetFilePointer` | `lseek` (FILE_BEGIN/CURRENT/END); a 64-bit offset when `distHi` is given; INVALID_SET_FILE_POINTER on error. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `CreateFileMappingA` | Win32 separates "create the mapping" from "show a piece". POSIX has only `mmap`. So the file handle is passed on and all the work is done in `MapViewOfFile` - no state has to be remembered between the calls. |
| function | `MapViewOfFile` | Read-only private `mmap` of the file (length = `bytes`, or the whole file when 0); remembered for `UnmapViewOfFile`. NULL on error. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `UnmapViewOfFile` | `munmap` of a mapping made by `MapViewOfFile` (its length looked up); FALSE for an unknown address. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetTickCount` | Milliseconds of a monotonic clock. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `timeGetTime` | The same as `GetTickCount`. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `QueryPerformanceCounter` | Win32 gives the counter and the frequency separately. Nanoseconds and a frequency of `1e9` are given, so the quotient comes out in seconds - as the calling code expects. |
| function | `QueryPerformanceFrequency` | Always 1e9 - the counter counts nanoseconds. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| EM_JS | `m2w_fps_limit` | `?fps=N` - an artificial frame limit for tests: loop turns faster than 1000/N ms are skipped, as on a slow monitor. |
| EM_JS | `m2w_events_from_loop` | `?events=loop` - the old road of the event frame counter (one event frame per loop turn), for A/B (stage_port.py). |
| function | `M2W_EventsFromLoop` | 1 = movement events counted as in the original (one frame per loop turn) instead of from time - the A/B switch, read once. |
| function | `M2W_LoopStillSleeping` | Whether the main loop should skip this turn: a wait requested by `Sleep` is still running, or the artificial frame limit `?fps=N` says less than 1000/N ms (minus 1 ms of slack) passed since the last turn *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `Sleep` | Does not block (the browser thread must not): stores a deadline that the main loop honours (`M2W_LoopStillSleeping`); logs sleeps of 20 ms or more (first 20). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetLastError` | `errno` of the last failed POSIX call. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `OutputDebugStringA` | Writes the text to stderr (the browser console). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `MessageBoxA` | No modal window: logs "[MessageBox] caption: text" to stderr and returns IDOK (1). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetModuleFileNameA` | The conventional name "/metin2.wasm" (there is no executable path); 0 if it does not fit. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `FindFirstFileA` | `opendir` of the pattern's directory (the mask is ignored - TMP4 uses only `*` and `*.*`) and the first entry; INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE on error or an empty directory. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `FindNextFileA` | The next `readdir` entry: name and FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY; FALSE at the end. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `FindClose` | `closedir` and frees the search state. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetTempPathA` | "/tmp/"; returns the size needed when the buffer is too small. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetTempFileNameA` | `path` + `prefix` + 4 hex digits + ".tmp" (a counter when `unique` is 0); does not create the file. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GetSystemInfo` | Page size from `sysconf`, ONE processor, allocation granularity 65536 (a wasm memory page). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GlobalAlloc` | `calloc` with GMEM_ZEROINIT, else `malloc`; the handle IS the pointer. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `GlobalFree` | `free`; returns NULL (success). *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `CopyFileA` | Copying a file. `bFailIfExists` kept exactly as in Win32: when true, an existing target file is **not** overwritten and the function returns false. *(from win32_compat.h)* |
| function | `_chdir` | `chdir`. *(from win32_compat.h)* |

## `win32_compat.h`

win32_compat.h - the Win32 -> POSIX/emscripten compatibility layer for the TMP4 port. WHAT FOR: `EterBase` (and the other TMP4 layers) is VS6-era code that reaches for `windows.h`. Instead of rewriting calls in hundreds of places, I provide the **twenty** functions the code really uses. The number is measured, not guessed - a `grep` for Win32 symbols in the whole of `EterBase` gives 20 different n

| kind | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| macro | `__declspec` | MSVC attributes - dropped. |
| function | `HandleToFd` | A file handle. Win32 passes a `HANDLE`, POSIX a descriptor - I keep the descriptor **shifted by one**, so that `fd == 0` does not collide with `NULL`. |
| function | `FdToHandle` | The inverse of `HandleToFd`. |
| struct | `Mapping` | Remembered mappings, so that `UnmapViewOfFile` knows the length. Win32 does not require it, POSIX `munmap` does - a real difference between the interfaces, not decoration. |
| function | `FindMapping` | The remembered mapping starting at `addr`, or NULL. |
| function | `RememberMapping` | Remembers a mapping made by `MapViewOfFile`. |
| function | `ForgetMapping` | Forgets the mapping at `addr` (after `munmap`). |
| function | `CreateFileA` | POSIX `open`: GENERIC_READ/WRITE -> O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY/O_RDWR, CREATE_ALWAYS -> O_CREAT\|O_TRUNC; the path goes through `M2W_ResolvePathCase` (read) or `M2W_PosixPath` (write). INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE on error. |
| function | `CloseHandle` | `close` of the file descriptor; FALSE for INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE or NULL. |
| function | `ReadFile` | `read` up to `toRead` bytes; `*read` = bytes read (0 on error). |
| function | `WriteFile` | `write` of `toWrite` bytes; `*written` = bytes written (0 on error). |
| function | `GetFileSize` | `fstat` size - low 32 bits returned, high 32 in `*hi`; INVALID_FILE_SIZE on error. |
| function | `SetFilePointer` | `lseek` (FILE_BEGIN/CURRENT/END); a 64-bit offset when `distHi` is given; INVALID_SET_FILE_POINTER on error. |
| function | `CreateFileMappingA` | Win32 separates "create the mapping" from "show a piece". POSIX has only `mmap`. So the file handle is passed on and all the work is done in `MapViewOfFile` - no state has to be remembered between the calls. *(from win32_compat.cpp)* |
| function | `MapViewOfFile` | Read-only private `mmap` of the file (length = `bytes`, or the whole file when 0); remembered for `UnmapViewOfFile`. NULL on error. |
| function | `UnmapViewOfFile` | `munmap` of a mapping made by `MapViewOfFile` (its length looked up); FALSE for an unknown address. |
| function | `GetTickCount` | Milliseconds of a monotonic clock. |
| function | `timeGetTime` | The same as `GetTickCount`. |
| function | `QueryPerformanceCounter` | Win32 gives the counter and the frequency separately. Nanoseconds and a frequency of `1e9` are given, so the quotient comes out in seconds - as the calling code expects. *(from win32_compat.cpp)* |
| function | `QueryPerformanceFrequency` | Always 1e9 - the counter counts nanoseconds. |
| function | `Sleep` | Does not block (the browser thread must not): stores a deadline that the main loop honours (`M2W_LoopStillSleeping`); logs sleeps of 20 ms or more (first 20). |
| function | `M2W_LoopStillSleeping` | Whether the main loop should skip this turn: a wait requested by `Sleep` is still running, or the artificial frame limit `?fps=N` says less than 1000/N ms (minus 1 ms of slack) passed since the last turn |
| function | `GetLastError` | `errno` of the last failed POSIX call. |
| function | `OutputDebugStringA` | Writes the text to stderr (the browser console). |

## `windows.h`

windows.h - a REDIRECT for the TMP4 port. TMP4 code includes this header directly. Instead of rewriting hundreds of #include directives, I provide a file with this name that pulls in our compatibility layer. That keeps the TMP4 sources UNTOUCHED - and the less we touch them, the easier it will be to take in fixes from upstream.

## `windowsx.h`

windowsx.h - helper macros for handling window messages. `MSWindow.cpp` pulls this header in for macros like `GET_X_LPARAM`. In the browser there is no message loop - events come from the canvas - so the file is empty, and the macros themselves I will add when the compiler asks for them (and it is known which are really used).

## `winsock.h`

winsock.h - a REDIRECT for the TMP4 port. TMP4 code includes this header directly. Instead of rewriting hundreds of #include directives, I provide a file with this name that pulls in our compatibility layer. That keeps the TMP4 sources UNTOUCHED - and the less we touch them, the easier it will be to take in fixes from upstream.

## `winuser.h`

winuser.h - a redirect to the compatibility layer. A header TMP4 code pulls in directly. In Win32 it belongs to the `windows.h` family; here its content lives in `win32_compat.h`.

## `wtypes.h`

wtypes.h - a REDIRECT for the TMP4 port (COM headers).
