## `runtime.js` - page-side functions (`m2w.*`)

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `m2w.isLocalPage` | True on a page opened from this machine (file://, localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]) - where the diagnostic options are allowed. |
| `m2w.uiScale` | GUI scale: the game sees a LOGICAL screen = physical pixels / scale (`?scale=2` -> windows and fonts 2x larger), while the canvas and the drawing buffer stay PHYSICAL - the 3D world in full resolution, interface quads multiplied in the shader (gl_device.cpp), fonts baked at `lfHeight * scale` (platform_text.cpp), so letters are sharp, not enlarged. Only scales with baked fonts are allowed (tools/bake_fonts.py SKALE); the choice is remembered in localStorage `m2w.scale`. Cached after the first call. |
| `m2w.effectiveDpr` | Effective device pixel ratio with the RESOLUTION CAP: the drawing buffer does not exceed 1920x1080 (user: "Full HD at most"). On a larger screen the game gets 1080p and the browser stretches the canvas (CSS 100%) over the whole area - like the Windows client at 1920x1080 on a 4K monitor. One factor, min(devicePixelRatio, 1920 / CSS width, 1080 / CSS height), goes through EVERY screen measure (GetSystemMetrics, desktop mode, canvas size, mouse). `?max=WxH` changes the limit, `?max=0` removes it. |
| `m2w.cssToBufferRatio` | LOGICAL pixels per CSS pixel: effective dpr / GUI scale. Every "screen size" the game asks for goes through this. |
| `m2w.cursorMode` | Cursor mode from the address: 1 = software (the game draws it, browser cursor hidden - cursor_web.cpp), 2 = hardware (CSS), 0 = not given (metin2.cfg decides). |
| `m2w.canvasState` | Canvas state for WM_SIZE: what = 0 width, 1 height (both in LOGICAL pixels), 2 = the tab is hidden (1/0). The DISPLAYED size, not the buffer: `canvas.width/height` is the buffer we set at Reset, so after a window resize it looked unchanged, WM_SIZE never went out and a 1280x150 image was stretched over 1253x918. PHYSICAL pixels: CSS pixels at 150 % Windows scaling gave a 1677x1278 buffer stretched to 2516x1917 - every glyph blurred 1.5x. `GetSystemMetrics` multiplies by the same ratio, so both measures agree. |
| `m2w.windowSize` | Window (= screen) size in LOGICAL pixels for GetSystemMetrics. `innerWidth/innerHeight` are CSS pixels; without the ratio the game got a smaller "screen" than the monitor, drew a smaller buffer and the browser stretched it - blurred text at 150 % Windows scaling. |
| `m2w.safeUrl` | `u` as an absolute address when it is an http(s) page (relative addresses are resolved against this page), '' otherwise. Everything that navigates to an address from outside - `?return=`, the in-game browser - goes through here: a `javascript:` or `data:` address would run code in the player's page (a link to the real site with `?return=javascript:...`). |
| `m2w.quit` | What the page does after PostQuitMessage (user decision): first try to close the tab, and when the browser refuses (only a tab opened by script may close itself) go back where the player came from - `?return=`, `m2w.config.returnUrl` set by the page, or `document.referrer` on the same origin - and with none of these, show a message. The client carries NO page address of its own; that is a deployment setting. |
| `m2w.heapBytes` | Copies `bytes` (a Uint8Array, or null) into a new `malloc` buffer and writes its length under `piLength`; returns the pointer, or 0 (length 0) for null. The caller frees it. |
| `m2w.heapString` | `s` as a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string in a new `malloc` buffer (the caller frees it). |
| `m2w.heapInts` | Writes the numbers of `values` as 32-bit ints from address `p` on. |
| `m2w.heapDoubles` | Writes the numbers of `values` as doubles from address `p` on. |
| `m2w.shouldRun` | 0 when the address says `?run=0` (do not start the client), else 1 - also 1 when the page replaced `m2w.options` with its own object. |
| `m2w.eventsStart` | Installs the listeners on the canvas and the window. Safe to repeat; does nothing until the canvas exists. |
| `m2w.eventPoll` | Next queued event `{k, w, x, y}` or null. |
| `m2w.eventPollInto` | Takes one event off the queue into four ints at `pData` (message, `wParam`, x, y); 0 when the queue is empty, else 1. |
| `m2w.mouseSet` | Moves the virtual cursor to (x, y) - what `SetCursorPos` does; 0 before the events are installed. |
| `m2w.pumpNow` | Hands the queued messages to the game now (`M2W_PumpMessagesNow`, the `CPythonApplication::Loop` patch in tools/stage_port.py); returns how many were taken - 0 before the main loop runs or the module is ready. |
| `m2w.keysStart` | Installs the key-state table (`globalThis.m2w_keys`, 256 bytes indexed by VK code) and the `keydown` / `keyup` / `blur` listeners that fill it. Kept in JavaScript because that is where the events arrive; a query from C++ is one boundary crossing per key per frame, and there are few pollers. |
| `m2w.keyPressed` | Whether the key with this VK code is down now (0/1). |
| `m2w.moviePlay` | Puts a `<video>` overlay over the page and plays `bytes` (a copy taken by the bridge - a `Blob` cannot hold a view of the wasm heap, which moves whenever memory grows); `name` only for the warning. |
| `m2w.cursorCanvas` | The canvas element, if the page has one. |
| `m2w.cursorRefresh` | Writes `canvas.style.cursor` from the current state. CAMERA-TURN FALLBACK: when the browser refuses the pointer lock (e.g. an app panel: "root document not valid for pointer lock") the real cursor follows the hand; hiding it then would make it reappear wherever it got to on release ("the cursor jumps", user). So during a camera drag with NO lock (`lockBroken`) it stays visible (in the "turn camera" shape the game just set). A lock REQUESTED but not yet granted counts as a lock, or the cursor is visible at the moment the browser warps it to the centre. |
| `m2w.cursorSet` | The game set a shape: remember it and apply it when the cursor is shown. The last value is remembered so that `cursorVisible(1)` returns to it (earlier it set '' and lost the shape). |
| `m2w.cursorVisible` | `ShowCursor`: visible (1) or hidden (0). |
| `m2w.dikStart` | Installs the listeners and the table. Safe to repeat. |
| `m2w.browserLanguage` | The language to play in, in this order: `?lang=` (remembered), then localStorage `m2/lang`, then `?deflang=`, then the browser languages, finally `en`. Returns {lang, codePage}. |
| `m2w.loadFont` | Registers `/tahoma.ttf` from the preloaded package (MEMFS, before main) as the browser font "Tahoma". MEASURED, not guessed: the game asks for UI_DEF_FONT = "Tahoma:12", `CreateFontIndirectA` (platform_text.cpp) turns it into CSS `font-family: "Tahoma"` and LEAVES THE CHOICE TO THE BROWSER - without our own file the result depends on what the system substitutes (user: "the font is awful"). Loading is asynchronous (`FontFace.load()`), but the bytes are already in memory - parsing 919 kB takes milliseconds, and Python start-up gives plenty of slack. |
| `m2w.bridgeStart` | Decides where the bridge is and tells SOCKFS the URL scheme. Runs once, at the first `connect()`. TWO DEPLOYMENTS, both real: (1) a LOCAL page (file://, localhost, 127.0.0.1) - the bridge stands next to it on its own port 11496; (2) a page FROM A SERVER (nginx) - the bridge has no address of its own, it goes through the page's host and port and the web server forwards it, hence `location.host` WITH the port. Over HTTPS `wss://` is required: the browser refuses a plain WebSocket from an encrypted page. An explicit address wins over everything: `?bridge=` (local pages only - see m2w.options), then `m2w.config.bridge` (written into site/client.html by link_client.py from private/bridge.txt - page on a hosting, proxy elsewhere). Accepted with or without a scheme: "ws://host:port", "wss://host", "host:port", "host". |
| `m2w.addressViaBridge` | Registers `<bridge host>/to/<target>` in emscripten's name table and returns the fake address it was given, packed like `sin_addr` (network order: first octet in the lowest byte). 0 when the table refused. |
| `m2w.webbrowserShow` | Creates the iframe if needed, places it at (left, top, right, bottom) CSS pixels and loads `url`. Returns 1 when the frame exists; whether the PAGE shows in it depends on the shop's headers (see the .cpp). |
| `m2w.webbrowserMove` | Moves and resizes the frame to (left, top, right, bottom) CSS pixels; nothing before the first show. |
| `m2w.webbrowserHide` | Hides the frame and unloads the page on purpose: a hidden frame would live on, play sound and keep the shop's connections. |
| `m2w.webbrowserDestroy` | Removes the frame from the page for good (the next show creates a new one). |
| `m2w.fetchSync` | Downloads `url` SYNCHRONOUSLY and returns a Uint8Array, or null: a synchronous XMLHttpRequest on the main thread - not Asyncify, not SharedArrayBuffer, both cost more than needed, and it does NOT change the order of game code, which assumes the file is ready right after `fopen`. `responseType = 'arraybuffer'` is ILLEGAL on a synchronous request, so the bytes come as text through `charset=x-user-defined`, which maps every byte to U+F700+byte and `& 0xFF` gives the byte back - for 0x80-0x9F too. (ISO-8859-1, tried first, is aliased to windows-1252 by the WHATWG standard and remaps 0x80-0x9F: byte 0x94 came out as 0x1D.) `expected` > 0 is the chunk size from the manifest: the text API does BOM sniffing despite the charset, and a chunk starting with FE FF / FF FE / EF BB BF came back decoded as UTF-16/UTF-8 with another length (measured: chunk 195, 4194304 B -> 2097151 "characters", 44 files read from shifted places). Refusing beats garbage. Compared with the manifest size, not Content-Length (under gzip that counts bytes on the wire). build_corpus.py makes sure no chunk starts with a BOM; this is the second line. |
| `m2w.chunkCacheStart` | Creates the chunk cache once (`m2w.chunks`, budget `budgetMB` MB) with its eviction rule and opens the Cache Storage `m2w-corpus` (null where the origin has none - then chunks do not survive the session). |
| `m2w.chunkFromCache` | SYNCHRONOUS read from the page memory: the chunk's bytes or null. This is the whole gain of background fetching - a chunk already here costs the game no round trip. |
| `m2w.chunkCachePut` | Puts a chunk the game just read (blocking fetch) into the page memory, marked as used, and keeps the budget. |
| `m2w.chunkInBackground` | Fetches a chunk IN THE BACKGROUND - Cache Storage first, then the network - into the page memory. UPPER BOUND IN FLIGHT: the synchronous road never yields, so successive `Get()` calls in one frame kept adding 3 fetches each - 52 measured at once; the browser has 6 sockets per server, the fetches held them with bodies nobody read, and the synchronous XHR waited for a socket exactly 20.0 s (7 x 20 s = 140 of 145 s of loading). Two from here + two from the prefetch (a separate counter so neither starves the other) = 4 of 6; the XHR always has one free. |
| `m2w.prefetchStart` | PREFETCH IN THE RECORDED ORDER. `<corpus>/order.txt` (tools/chunk_order.py) lists chunk hashes in the order the game reached for them at login and entering the village (recorded once through `m2w.corpus.order`). From page start they are fetched in that order, two at a time, into the page memory and Cache Storage. SLIDING WINDOW: the HTTP cache proved UNRELIABLE (measured: after 400 MB fetched in 2 s the synchronous XHR still went to the network despite `immutable`), and Cache Storage cannot be read synchronously. The only thing that spares the game is a chunk lying in `map` BEFORE it asks. So the prefetch downloads nothing it has no budget for: it waits until the game USES (reads from memory) the oldest chunks, evicts them, and only then fetches the next. With the game reading in the same order the prefetch stays one budget (m2w.corpusBudget: 96-512 MB = 24-128 chunks) ahead. When the game left the recorded path and used nothing for 15 s, the oldest chunk is evicted anyway - or the prefetch would stand on unwanted chunks all session. `?noprefetch=1` disables it. Progress: `m2w.prefetch` and the `Module.setStatus` bar before entering the game. |
| `m2w.chunkList` | Hands the page the list of all chunk hashes and the corpus address (preload.js downloads the rest into Cache Storage, from which the next start's prefetch reads it into memory. The Service Worker does NOT see the synchronous XHR, see below). |
| `m2w.chunkCounter` | Counters for the report: 0 from memory, 1 from storage, 2 from network, 3 chunks held, 4 MB held. |
| `m2w.corpusBudget` | Chunk memory budget in MB (`?corpusMB=` wins; otherwise by the device's memory). Until the measurement it was 96. Measured with a headless Edge, login + village, 90 s: the game uses ~102 chunks (~408 MB), and with 96 MB it evicted chunks it needed again a moment later - 138 BLOCKING downloads on a SECOND start (89 from the network, 4.8 s of frozen main thread on localhost); 256 MB -> 75 (62 from the network, 2.8 s); 512 MB -> 22 (0 from the network, 0.6 s), also on a first start 22 instead of 137. A Service Worker does not help here: it does not see the synchronous XHR at all. `navigator.deviceMemory` is the RAM in GB rounded down and capped at 8 (Chromium; Firefox and Safari give none). |
| `m2w.corpusUrl` | Corpus address with a trailing slash (`?corpus=`, default corpus/). |
| `m2w.chunkUsed` | Records the first use of a chunk (tools/chunk_order.py reads `m2w.corpus.order` from the console after a session). |
| `m2w.textCanvasCreate` | Creates a canvas of the given size and returns its index. |
| `m2w.textCanvasFont` | Sets the CSS font of text canvas `id` (baseline at the top). |
| `m2w.textMeasure` | Advance width of `text` in CSS pixels, in the canvas font. |
| `m2w.textMeasureThree` | Width, left and right bounding box of `text` - three numbers from one `TextMetrics` (one boundary crossing instead of three). |
| `m2w.textMeasurePrefixes` | REAL KERNING: cumulative width after every prefix of `text`, so the difference of two neighbours is the width of a character IN ITS NEIGHBOURHOOD - measured in isolation, "T" next to "y" and "T" next to "l" would come out the same, and the strings looked "crooked" (user). |
| `m2w.textBboxRight` | Right edge of `text`'s ink (`actualBoundingBoxRight`), or its width where the browser does not report it. |
| `m2w.textHeight` | Ink height of `text` (ascent + descent of its bounding box). |
| `m2w.textLineHeight` | FULL LINE height of the font, NOT of a particular string: `GrpFontTexture::UpdateCharacterInfomation` packs every character into the atlas in a cell as high as `GetTextExtentPoint32` says. Real GDI returns the line height (ascent + descent + internal leading); we used to return the nominal size (`lfHeight`), without room for descenders, so with `textBaseline='top'` a "y" spilled into the NEXT atlas row and showed up as a stray dot under an unrelated string (user report). `fontBoundingBoxAscent/Descent` measure the whole font; the "Mjpqy" probe is the fallback for browsers without those fields. |
| `m2w.textDraw` | Draws `text` at (x, y); with `opaque` the background is filled first, from the text down to the bottom of the canvas (GDI OPAQUE semantics). |
| `m2w.textReadRows` | Reads the rectangle [x0, x1) x [y0, y1) of the canvas into the DIB (`target` = wasm address, `stride` = DIB width) as BGRA - the step that hands the picture to TMP4 under the pointer from `CreateDIBSection`. Only the touched rectangle: the first version copied the whole 512x512 atlas for EVERY new character - a `getImageData` plus about a million writes per letter, thirty new chat characters = thirty million writes in one frame, stutter at every new name. Only columns of THIS character: a full-width copy after every `TextOutW` let a "y" (ink one pixel LEFT of its origin) permanently overwrite the "L" packed before it - the atlas has no gutter. Anti-aliasing threshold: `getImageData` returns un-premultiplied colour, so a pixel barely touched is (255,255,255,a=2) and the engine's "blue != 0" binarisation turned every faint edge into a full dot; pixels under alpha 8 are dropped here (lowered from 64 in 291h, when the dots proved to be the overwrite above, not the halo). |
| `m2w.soundStartSource` | Starts a buffer in a slot; shared by an immediate play and by a decode that has just finished. `generation` guards the `onended` callback: a slot re-allocated in the meantime belongs to somebody else. |
| `m2w.soundStart` | Creates the context and `slots` node pairs. `equalpower` panning IS the provider TMP4 chose ("Miles Fast 2D Positional Audio": pan and volume, no HRTF); `refDistance` 1 because C++ divides positions by the sound scale (200) first - see sound_web.cpp, "Design". |
| `m2w.soundLoad` | Hands the bytes of a file to the decoder. 1 = buffer ready, 0 = decoding (slots that wait for this crc start when it finishes), -1 = cannot. `bytes` must be a COPY: `decodeAudioData` detaches the buffer it gets and a piece of the wasm heap must never be detached. |
| `m2w.soundPlay` | Plays a file in a slot: now if decoded, when the decode finishes if not yet, never if unknown or broken. |
| `m2w.soundStop` | Stops slot `slot` at once and forgets a pending start (bumps the generation, so a late `onended` does nothing). |
| `m2w.soundSlotFree` | 1 when nothing plays in the slot and nothing waits for a decode. |
| `m2w.soundVolume` | Sets the slot's gain (0..1) from now on. |
| `m2w.soundPosition` | Source position relative to the listener (C++ already divided by the scale and flipped Z). |
| `m2w.soundListenerPosition` | Listener position alone; TMP4 keeps it apart from the direction (`SetListenerPosition` vs `SetListenerDirection`) and calls them from different places, so here too they are two functions. |
| `m2w.soundListenerDirection` | Listener direction alone - the counterpart of `AIL_set_3D_orientation`. |
| `m2w.imeEnable` | Focuses (`enabled`) or blurs the `m2w_ime` element; nothing when the page has none (today no page does). |
| `m2w.fpsLimit` | `?fps=N` as a number, 0 when absent or not positive. |
| `m2w.eventsFromLoop` | 1 when `?events=loop` is in the address. |

|---|---|
| `tools/animation_review.py` | Survey of the animations in the corpus: curve shapes, degrees, track group members, text tracks. A measurement BEFORE writing the sampling - so as to write only what the data really carries, and to know what is NOT there. |

| `tools/bake_speedtree.py` | Builds and runs the SpeedTree tree baker. |

| `tools/build_eterbase.py` | Builds `build/port/lib/libeterbase.a` FROM SCRATCH, from source. |
| `tools/build_eterpack.py` | Builds `build/port/lib/libeterpack.a` FROM SCRATCH, from source. |

| `tools/build_lzo.py` | Builds `build/port/lib/liblzo.a` FROM SCRATCH, from the LZO 2.10 sources. |
| `tools/build_python.py` | build_python.py - CPython 3.13 for wasm32-emscripten, the game's script engine. |
| `tools/check_corpus.py` | check_corpus.py - checks the WHOLE client corpus byte for byte. |
| `tools/chunk_order.py` | chunk_order.py - the order in which corpus chunks are prefetched. |
| `tools/cursors.py` | cursors.py - the game's mouse cursors (`.cur` from the TMP4 resources) as PNG with their hotspot, for the client data package (`data/cursors/`). |
| `tools/division.py` | division.py - gives Python 2 back its division, but only where it can be SHOWN. |
| `tools/dxt_crosscheck.py` | CROSS-check of DXT decompression with an independent decoder (Pillow). |
| `tools/gates/check_behaviour.py` | Behaviour gate without a game server: drive the client headless to the login screen and compare what it did with a recorded baseline. |
| `tools/gates/check_declared.py` | Every `/// Declared only` label in compat/*.h must be true. |
| `tools/gates/check_docs.py` | Every function of the port layer has a `///` description - checked by the compiler. |
| `tools/gates/check_glsl.py` | Shader-composer gate for Phase C groups 6-7: compat/tests/glsl_dump.cpp prints the GLSL that compat/d3d8_fixedfunc.cpp generates for 1141 pipeline keys; this compares it with the recorded dump. |
| `tools/gates/check_link.py` | Gate on the LINKED client, where the object-level baseline is blind. |
| `tools/gates/check_metrics.py` | Readability metrics for compat (plan phase C gate). |
| `tools/gates/check_names.py` | Find old names anywhere in our layer (plan phase A/B/E gate). |
| `tools/gates/check_probe.py` | Model-chain gate without a game server (Phase C group 5): the model probe (`?modelprobe=N`, custom_draw.cpp) draws N instances of a .gr2 model on the login screen - our reader, pose, skinning and custom draw, nothing of the game's own drawing - and with `?probehash=F` prints an FNV-1a hash of the canvas after the F-th probe frame (the frame is cleared first, because the login screen behind it is not deterministic). |
| `tools/gates/common.py` | Shared helpers for the quality gates (tools/gates). |
| `tools/gates/reference.py` | Build docs/REFERENCE.md from the code (plan phase W) and gate on missing docs. |
| `tools/gates/run_tests.py` | Build and run the layer's unit tests (compat/tests/*_test.cpp) under node. |
| `tools/gr2.py` | gr2.py - parsing a Granny `.gr2` file. |
| `tools/link_client.py` | link_client.py - THE FIRST LINK OF THE WHOLE. |
| `tools/oodle1.py` | oodle1.py - unpacking `.gr2` sections packed with the Oodle1 codec. |
| `tools/package.py` | package.py - the ready directory to upload. |
| `tools/repair_gr2.py` | repair_gr2.py - the .gr2 files our Oodle1 does not unpack, saved with raw sections by the real granny2.dll. |
| `tools/rewrite_scripts.py` | rewrite_scripts.py - the game scripts from Python 2 to Python 3. |
| `tools/script_patches.py` | script_patches.py - what `lib2to3` will NOT do. |
| `tools/site_server.py` | site_server.py - serves the built client on 127.0.0.1, and ONLY the client. |
| `tools/speedtree_bake/measurements/elevation.py` | SpeedTree leaf-card measurement: reads the corner dumps el_<elevation>.txt of the baker for elevations -90..90 and fits each card corner as a + b cos(el) + c sin(el), printing the fit error - how the leaf cards turn with the camera elevation. |
| `tools/speedtree_bake/measurements/frame.py` | SpeedTree leaf-card measurement: expresses the card edges and centres of every camera dump kam_*.txt in the camera frame (right, up, forward), to see how the cards face the camera. |
| `tools/speedtree_bake/measurements/kabsch2.py` | SpeedTree leaf-card measurement: for every camera dump kam_<x>_<y>_<z>.txt, fits the linear map from the base corners (az 0, el 0) and compares it with candidate rotations Rz(az), Rz(az)Ry(+-el), Rz(az)Ry(+-el/2), printing the error of each. |
| `tools/speedtree_bake/measurements/model.py` | SpeedTree leaf-card measurement: derives each card's rotation axis angle rho from the elevation dumps and checks the model corner(az, el) = Rz(az) Rz(rho) Ry(-el) Rz(-rho) corner(0, 0) against every dump, printing the worst error. |
| `tools/spt.py` | spt.py - parsing `.spt` files, i.e. the SpeedTree TREE RECIPE. |
| `tools/stage_port.py` | stage_port.py - assembles the port's source tree from two parts. |
| `tools/uiscript_from_client.py` | uiscript_from_client.py - the interface window descriptions, extracted and rewritten. |
| `tools/unpack_packs.py` | unpack_packs.py - extracts the scripts and data from the client packs. |
| `tools/webfs.py` | webfs.py - reads a data corpus in the M2WF format (by default `build/port/corpus`, written by build_corpus.py; or pass another directory). |
| `tools/workspace.py` | workspace.py - where the build finds its inputs and puts its outputs. |

## Tool functions

### `tools/animation_review.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `file_list` | Paths of the corpus .gr2 files, optionally only those whose path contains `pattern` (case-insensitive). |

Block comments are tracked across lines: an unbalanced `(` in `/* see Reset( */` would otherwise start a fold that swallows every following declaration in the file (reviewer review). |

### `tools/gr2.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `Section.__init__` | Reads one 44-byte section entry at `offset`: compression, data offset, packed/unpacked size, alignment, the two Oodle1 split points, relocation and marshalling tables. |
| `Section.compression_name` | Name of the section's compression (e.g. Oodle1), or "unknown N". |
| `Section.description` | One line: compression, packed -> unpacked size, the 16/8 split points and the relocation count. |
| `GrannyFile.__init__` | Parses the file header: magic (variant), header format (packed ones are refused), version, sizes, root type and root object pointers, and the section table; on a problem sets `error` instead of raising. |
| `GrannyFile.raw_section` | The section's bytes AS THEY LIE IN THE FILE - still packed. |
| `Pointer.__init__` | A pointer inside the file: section number and offset in it. |
| `Pointer.shift_by` | The pointer moved by `o` bytes within the same section. |
| `Pointer.__eq__` | Equal when both section and offset are equal. |
| `Pointer.__hash__` | Hash of (section, offset), so pointers can key dicts. |
| `Pointer.__repr__` | `section:offset` in hex, e.g. `2:0000a1c0`. |
| `Field.__init__` | One member description of a type: kind, name, sub-type pointer, array width and the extra words. |
| `Field.kind_name` | Name of the member kind, or "unknown N". |
| `Field.multiplicity` | How many elements. Zero and one mean the same: one element. |
| `Field.__repr__` | `kind name`, with `[width]` for arrays. |
| `Image.__init__` | Unpacks the sections (raw ones padded, Oodle1 ones decompressed; only `sections_only` when given, the others left as None) and builds the relocation map (section, offset) -> target pointer. |
| `Image.data_bytes` | `how_many` bytes at pointer `ptr`; ValueError when the section was not unpacked or the read leaves it. |
| `Image.number` | One `struct` value of format `format` at pointer `ptr`. |
| `Image.pointer` | The pointer stored at address `ptr` - or None when null. |
| `Image.text_value` | The string pointed to from address `ptr` (zero-terminated). |
| `Image.type_desc` | The list of fields of the type at address `ptr`. |
| `Image.type_size` | How many bytes an object described by the type at `ptr` takes. |
| `Image.field_size` | Size in bytes of a member: its type's size for inline members, the kind's fixed size otherwise, times the array width. |
| `Image.obj` | The object at `obj_ptr` read according to the type description at `type_ptr`. |
| `Image.value_of` | The value of one member at `p` as plain Python: inline objects and references followed up to `depth` levels, arrays cut at `array_limit`, strings, transforms and numbers decoded; a placeholder string where the depth runs out. |
| `Image.inline_array` | `how_many` inline objects of type `type_desc` from `target` (at most `array_limit`, then a "... N more" marker); a placeholder at depth 0. |
| `Image.reference_array` | `how_many` references (4-byte pointers) from `target`, each followed to an object of type `type_desc` (at most `array_limit`); a placeholder at depth 0. |
| `Node.__init__` | A typed object in the unpacked file: type pointer and object pointer. |
| `Node.field_list` | The member list of the node's type. |
| `Node.where` | (field description, field address) - or an exception when there is no such field. |
| `Node.__contains__` | True when the node's type has a member called `name`. |
| `Node.__getitem__` | The value of a field. Objects and arrays of objects come out as nodes. |
| `Node.lookup` | The node as a dict (see `Image.obj`), `depth` levels deep, arrays cut at `limit`. |
| `Node.__repr__` | `Node(type @ pointer)`. |
| `VariantArray.__init__` | An array of `how_many` elements of type `type_desc` starting at `ptr` (a variant array: the type travels with the data). |
| `VariantArray.__len__` | Number of elements. |
| `VariantArray.__getitem__` | Element `i` as a `Node` (negative indices count from the end); IndexError out of range. |
| `VariantArray.field_list` | The members of the element type ([] without a type). |
| `VariantArray.__repr__` | `VariantArray(count x size B, type_desc ...)`. |
| `root_node` | The root object of the file as a `Node`. |
| `walk` | Navigates the tree by a path string: `Meshes/0/PrimaryVertexData`. |
| `print_tree` | Prints a nested dict/list value as an indented tree to `file_path`. |
| `digest` | A short printable form of a leaf value (floats with %g). |
| `load_from_corpus` | Extracts a file from the streamed corpus (`build/port/corpus`, tools/webfs.py). |
| `load_file` | The bytes of `name`: a file on disk if it exists, else the corpus entry. |
| `open_file` | (GrannyFile, Image) of `name`; ValueError when the header cannot be parsed. |
| `cmd_header` | `gr2.py NAME`: prints the header and the section table; 1 on a bad file. |
| `cmd_type` | `--type NAME`: prints the root type's members with offsets, sizes and sub-type member names. |
| `cmd_tree` | `--tree NAME`: prints the root object as a tree. |
| `cmd_path` | `--path NAME PATH`: prints the node, variant array or list reached by PATH (e.g. Meshes/0/PrimaryVertexData). |
| `layout_signature` | The layout of one vertex as a tuple - for comparing files. |
| `verify_file` | Walks the WHOLE file and collects numbers. Raises an exception on a slip. |
| `cmd_check` | `--check [N] [PATTERN]`: walks the whole tree of N random corpus .gr2 files (seed 1), counts objects and vertex layouts, lists every failure; 1 when any file failed. |
| `main` | Command line: dispatches to the `cmd_*` commands; prints the usage without arguments. The Polish flag names from earlier still work. |

### `tools/link_client.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `tool_name` | Path of an emsdk tool: from PATH, else from the EMSDK directory; exits when it is nowhere. |
| `collect_objects` | Every .o under obj/gamelib (sorted per directory). |
| `strip_machine_paths` | Removes the paths of this machine from the JS glue: emscripten writes the data package under its full path (`PACKAGE_NAME`, a key used consistently, so replacing every occurrence keeps it working) and `// include:` comments naming the project and the temp folder. |
| `compile_entry` | The objects that belong to the link but not to the contract: `main_web.cpp` (the entry point) and `link_data.cpp` (data symbols the linker needs, e.g. `GrannyPNT332VertexType`). They are not in `build_gamelib.py`, because the contract asks what is MISSING, and neither provides anything to the game code. |
| `copy_site_scripts` | Copies sw.js and preload.js from site/ next to the page. |
| `main` | Links the whole client (objects + archives + the entry point) into client.wasm/client.js with a fixed hash seed, lists the stubs from the JS glue and the unexpected ones, then writes the page, the measuring shell and the crash reporter next to it. 1 on a failed compile or link. |
| `main.stubs_from_glue` | Names of the stubs (unresolved symbols) as the JS glue lists them (`missing function: NAME`) - read from the output, not the linker log. |
| `page_parses` | Does the JavaScript in the shell parse at all? |
| `summarize` | Prints the stubs GROUPED. The number alone says nothing - the difference between "Granny is missing" and "something I did not know about is missing" is the whole content of this measurement. |

### `tools/oodle1.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `BitReader.__init__` | Starts reading `data` at byte `start_pos`: the first byte split into its seven high bits (register) and the low bit (waiting outside). |
| `BitReader._byte` | The next input byte, or 0 past the end (the decoder stops by output size and may read a few bytes beyond the data). |
| `BitReader.load_register` | Shifts whole bytes in ("7+1" split) until the modulus exceeds 0x800000. |
| `BitReader.peek` | The next value on the scale [0, jeden) without consuming it (clamped to jeden - 1; 0 when the modulus is smaller than the scale). |
| `BitReader.consume` | Consumes the interval [min_z, min_z + span) of the scale `one_step`; the top interval takes the whole remaining modulus. |
| `BitReader.take` | A peek combined with consumption - for a uniformly distributed value. |
| `SymbolCoder.__init__` | An adaptive coder for `alphabet_size` values of which `unique_symbols` can occur: only the escape known, decay and renormalisation thresholds from the alphabet size. |
| `SymbolCoder._ensure_room` | Adds room in the tables when the active alphabet has outgrown the alphabet. |
| `SymbolCoder.split_range` | Reduces the weights of rarely used symbols until they drop out of the alphabet. |
| `SymbolCoder.normalize` | Divides the range [0,1) among the learned symbols. |
| `SymbolCoder.decode_symbol` | Decodes one symbol and updates the weights: renormalises (with decay) when due, then a known symbol or, after the escape, one from the not-yet-normalised tail or a brand new one read uniformly. |
| `Decompressor.code_group` | Which of the four header bytes covers length code `code` (groups of 16, code 64 in the last). |
| `Decompressor.__init__` | Sets up the LZ decoder from the three header words: window, literal alphabet and the 4 literal, 65 length and distance coders. |
| `Decompressor.step` | One call: a literal or a repeat. Returns the number of bytes. |
| `unpack_section` | Unpacks one `.gr2` section - up to THREE streams in turn. |
| `main` | `oodle1.py FILE [SECTION]`: decompresses the Oodle1 sections of a .gr2 (disk or corpus) and prints the size and first 16 bytes of each. |

### `tools/package.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `link_or_copy` | Puts `source` at `target` as a hard link (no extra space on NTFS), or a copy when linking fails. |
| `build` | Runs build_client_data.py (optionally `--no-private`) and link_client.py; False when either fails or prints an error line. |
| `page` | Builds dist/site/: the data package WITHOUT private files (refuses when loginInfo.xml is still in it), the page files and the corpus; then restores the local package with the private files. 1 on an error. |
| `main` | Builds dist/site/ (`--site`, the default); returns its exit code. |

### `tools/repair_gr2.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `falls` | True when our decoder cannot unpack one of the sections. |
| `run_helper` | Runs repair_gr2.exe, retrying while Windows refuses to start it: a freshly built executable is held by the antivirus scan (WinError 32) - measured in the clean-clone trials for more than 10 s, so it waits up to `wait_seconds` with growing pauses before giving up. |
| `build_helper` | Builds repair_gr2.exe with tools/gr2_repair/build.bat in the MSVC x86 environment of `[tools] vcvars32`; False when MSVC is missing or the build fails. |
| `main` | Re-saves the .gr2 files our Oodle1 decoder cannot unpack through the real granny2.dll (raw sections) into the repaired directory; files already checked are skipped unless `--fresh`. |

### `tools/rewrite_scripts.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `count_divisions` | How many times the `/` operator occurs in the file - counting TOKENS, not text. |
| `parses_in_python3` | True when the file parses as Python 3. |
| `to_utf8` | Converts files from CP949 to UTF-8. Returns the number converted. |
| `match_names` | Renames files to the spelling the scripts really import. |
| `is_referenced` | Does any other script mention this file's name (without `.py`)? The game loads window descriptions and modules by name, so a name no script mentions is a file nothing loads. |
| `main` | Rewrites the game scripts from Python 2 to 3 (lib2to3 without the division fixer, then our script patches and the division pass) into a clean target, and reports files that still do not parse. |

### `tools/spt.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `_u32` | Little-endian uint32 at `pos`. |
| `_f32` | Little-endian float at `pos`. |
| `_credible_tag` | Whether something that looks like a tag stands at `pos`. |
| `_end` | True when `pos` is exactly the end of the data. |
| `_string_length` | If a length followed by content stands at `pos` - returns it. |
| `_parse_with_backtracking` | Finds a parse that ends EXACTLY at the end of the file. |

### `tools/webfs.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `Corpus.__init__` | Loads manifest.bin of the corpus in `directory`: header, chunk table, pack names and the file table (keyed by lower-case name, plus the original order); exits when it is not M2WF or does not end where it should. |
| `Corpus.chunk_path` | Path of chunk `iChunk` on disk (`<hash>.bin`). |
| `Corpus.chunk` | The content of a chunk. Keeps the LAST one in memory - the files of one pack lie next to each other, so consecutive reads usually hit the same one. |
| `Corpus.read_file` | The content of a game file, or `None` when it is not in the corpus. |
| `Corpus.verify_chunk` | Whether the chunk's hash agrees with its name. Returns (ok, reason). |
| `main` | Prints the manifest summary, how many chunks are on disk, the hash check of the first three chunks and a sample DDS read. |

### `tools/workspace.py`

| function | description |
|---|---|
| `_map_project_paths` | Adds `-ffile-prefix-map=<project>=.` to EMCC_CFLAGS (once). |
| `load_config` | Reads `webclient.toml` into a dict of sections; {} when the file is absent. |
| `setting` | The value of `[section] key`: the environment variable `env` first, then webclient.toml, then `default`. |
| `path_setting` | Like `setting`, for a path: a relative one is taken from the repository root. |
| `private_line` | The content of `build/port/private/<name>` stripped, '' when the file is absent. |
| `for_batch` | `path` unchanged when it can be written between double quotes in a cmd batch file; exits with an explanation when it holds a character cmd would act on (`"`, `%`, a line break) - a path from webclient.toml must not be able to end the quoting and add a command (security audit). |
| `server_address` | The game server address written into serverInfo.py: M2W_SERVER, then `[server] address`, then private/server.txt; '' when none is set. |
| `bridge_address` | The default bridge address put into the page: M2W_BRIDGE, then `[server] bridge`, then private/bridge.txt; '' means the page's own host. |
| `describe` | Prints every resolved path and whether it exists; the server and bridge only as set / not set (their values are private). |
